Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

#1829. Rotherham United v Oldham Athletic: Alex Bruce senses upturn in results is coming

After 15 games of the League Two season, the Millers are in the relegation zone.

But they have a win and a draw from their last two matches, and a two-goal victory at home to the Latics on Saturday would see the pair swap places, and Rotherham potentially leapfrogging others.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I think the last two performances have been something to build on – the Bromley away performance (an FA Cup win to end a ten-match winless streak) and then Grimsby," commented Millers coach Bruce.

"We've drawn too many games (seven in the league). A lot of those draws we know very easily could have been wins but it's easy for me to sit here and say that.

"Try to stay positive with it is the message to the players.

"I speak to managers all the time after games and they say, 'You've been a bit unlucky here.'

"But I don't want to make that excuse. I want to start getting results and I think the players do as well. My message is stay positive and the results will turn."

Asked what he see which gives him that confidence, the former Leeds United and Hull City defender replied: "Togetherness, a hunger to get out of the situation we're in. We know we need a good week to ten days, which can easily happen over the Christmas period with the amount of fixtures.

"It's just about creating positivity, picking out the things we need to improve on, the things we need to keep doing, and just keep hammering home that message.

"When you want to be successful at any football club you need everyone pulling in the right direction. That means players digging each other out, demanding better standards.

"If it gets to that point and we're all on the same page with that, that will be good."

Kian Spence has served a suspension and is one of a number of players back ahead of a busy time in the English footballing calendar, but Bruce will be mindful of how he juggles his resources.

"Mulls (top-scorer Paul Mullin) has had a bit of a back issue but he should be okay," he said.

"I've got players coming back from injury and suspension and we've got Saturday-Tuesday, with Barnet away, so I will pick a team for both games and look to try and freshen things up to keep a level of freshness about the starting XI."

#1826. When St Johnstone’s owner was offered square go by Rangers boss - and the call players still wind him up about

The amount of health and safety regulations required in the construction business nowadays means Geoff Brown is happy to be free the daily responsibility of running the family firm he established.

However, some form of welfare protection might have been helpful at the moment he saw Graeme Souness storming down the corridor towards him. “He was threatening to knock my block off,” he recalls.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

St Johnstone tea-lady Aggie Moffat had erupted because of the state in which Rangers had left the away dressing-room following a 1-1 draw in February 1991. She made sure Souness knew all about it. Brown was in the boardroom with the directors of both clubs when they heard a “serious commotion” in the foyer. The chairman went outside and was met by Souness, who ‘offered’ to take him outside.

“I did not make a noise of it at the time,” says Brown, who wonders what impact it might have had on Souness’ career had he agreed to take part in the square go the Ibrox manager was suggesting. “David Murray phoned me the following week to thank me for not making a noise about what happened,” he says.

Ownership of St Johnstone – his 38 years at the helm of the club is the longest any individual has owned a professional football club in Scotland in modern times – has afforded Brown, now 83, a ringside seat and very nearly active involvement in so many of the colourful incidents characterising the game in this country.

The Aggie incident is certainly included among those. Despite Brown keeping schtum about the threat from Souness at the time, it’s become one of Scottish football’s most well-rehearsed anecdotes.

Rightly so, because the so-called storm in a teacup had profound repercussions. Souness ended up citing the incident as one of the reasons he left Rangers for Liverpool shortly afterwards. Brown, by contrast, has not roamed far. Building houses for others occupied his time. After that proved profitable, it permitted him the luxury of time to devote to saving St Johnstone from the clutches of the receivers.

This was in 1986. The Perth club “were the strongest team in the country”. In other words, they were holding the rest of Scottish football up and were sitting plum last in the pile. One afternoon, shortly after Brown had agreed to take on all the debt, Tayside Safety Committee paid a visit. “There were about ten of them,” he recalls. “And they were put in the boardroom. I said: ‘I am sorry, what are you doing here?’

“One replied: ‘We are here to close down the club’. Notices had been given to the previous board that had never been passed on to us. They hadn’t met any of the safety standards at the last inspection, and nothing had been done after the inspections. So they were there to close the club down.”

Forty years and three major trophies later, Brown can reflect with a degree of satisfaction on his impact on football in his local area. But when he was presented with an Outstanding Contribution Award by first minister John Swinney at the Courier Business awards night in Dundee as recently as October, it was more his success as a housebuilder – he set up GS Brown Construction in 1970 – and charitable work that were being recognised.

As Brown was making his way in the construction business, he and his young family lived in a council house in Tulloch. It looked on to berry fields, owned by a farmer called Bruce McDiarmid.

Around twenty years later, as the new owner of St Johnstone FC, he met McDiarmid to negotiate a land deal. The trouble was, St Johnstone had no money to buy the fields on which it was being proposed they could build a new stadium. Asda’s interest in buying their then stadium, Muirton Park, came to light shortly afterwards.

Brown offered McDiarmid a 20 per cent stake in the club for the land, a deal the farmer’s lawyer advised him to reject. But McDiarmid accepted it. When Asda later offered £5 million for the Muirton Park site Brown cannily persuaded the supermarket firm to cover the cost of the new stadium instead. Some might still be under the impression, incorrect as it turns out, that McDiarmid gifted the land to St Johnstone, perhaps with the sole condition that they had to name the stadium after him.

“He certainly did not,” says Brown. “One way or the other, it did take a bit of persuading. I went with him to see his lawyer, who was older than Bruce. ‘No,’ the lawyer said. ‘You don’t really want that. If you are going to sell it, sell it’. Within a year I had Asda going to give us £5 million for Muirton Park. If you are sitting with 20 per cent of that you are not doing too bad…”

Brown’s new book is called Building My Life – shades of Alex Ferguson’s Managing My Life – but it could be called The Art of the Deal. It includes lots of wrangling and horse-trading, sometimes involving actual horses (As well as football, Brown is also a renowned racehorse owner). He doesn’t always come out on the right side of such negotiations, such as when the players were negotiating bonuses at the start of the 1998-99 season.

“That was a disaster,” he says. “The players – Paul Kane, Roddy Grant, Allan Preston – they were at (managing director) Stewart Duff because you always agree the bonuses at the start of the year. They are sitting arguing about bonuses for each potential position. And they come to 4th place. ‘4th place – are you happy with £250,000?’ Stewart asked. ‘Aye, go on then,’ I told him. ‘Now they are asking me for third place,’ he says.

“I said: ‘Stewart, they will never get third’. He says: ‘I agree with you. So should we just give them half a million?’”

Reader, they got third place, qualifying for the Uefa Cup in the process. “To this day the ones like Preston and Kane keep rubbing it in,” Brown says. “They tell me: ‘The one thing you got wrong with St Johnstone is that day you gave us too much money!’

“At that time, European football meant you ran at a loss. Because you’re hiring planes in the holiday period. Chartering a plane was expensive. Plus the (bonus) money we were paying players.”

Not that Brown regrets any of it. “It’s what you’re in it for, isn’t it?” he says. Now out of it after selling his majority stake in the club to Atlanta-based lawyer Adam Webb, he can enjoy attending games such as this weekend’s Tayside derby against Dundee United at Tannadice. At home games he sits in the Geoff Brown Stand. “The best bit is, whatever the scoreline, I can sleep afterwards,” he says.

Stewardship of a football club can take a toll, clearly. But Brown made some good friends, none better than Paul Sturrock. Of all the managers he employed, he was the one with whom he shared the closest relationship, to the extent that Brown’s wife Joyce regarded him as one of the family. “He’d let himself into the house and put the kettle on,” recalls Brown.

Even adversaries were entertained, such as Ron Dixon. The colourful one-time owner of Dundee actually bought Brown’s family home in St Madoes for those rare times when he was in Scotland. The Canadian complained to the St Johnstone owner that he’d been sold a pup when buying the Dens Park club. “They told me I was getting a sleeping giant!” he lamented. Brown told Sturrock. “Aye, they’re all lying in the cemetery!” the former Dundee United winger replied.

Memo to Dundonians of either hue: Brown has a few arch things to say about Dundee natives. However, citizens of the fair city of Perth will enjoy Brown’s book, likewise anyone partial to a classic rags-to-riches tale.

Building My Life: The Geoff Brown Story will be launched in the Centenary Suite at McDiarmid Park on November 30, from 6pm until 8pm. The book will be available in the St Johnstone club shop in Perth City Centre and at McDiarmid Park on match days.

"Since 2019, we have been continuously developing, refining and validating our proprietary football models and have established ourselves as a market leader in the football trading world," Godfrey told the Celtic website.

This means there is no conflict of interest with Celtic, who will have exclusivity in Scotland."

While Celtic have been left scrambling for loan signings on deadline day in recent windows, Godfrey says Pluto will "plan at least two windows in the future" as he backed the data and analytics to transform Celtic's recruitment.

"No scouting department has the resource to accurately analyse millions of players at the click of a button," he explained. "Our infrastructure allows us to track every single performance by every single player in professional and youth leagues across the world each week. We have automated internal flags that will alert our analysts every time a player reaches a certain threshold. These performance-related flags are agreed between us and Celtic to ensure that they are fully bespoke to the Club's needs as well as covering leagues that may previously have been out of reach.

"‘Will this player improve Celtic’s chances of winning?’ is the first and most important question which we will assess. Our model significantly outperforms global predictive markets in intercontinental and international tournaments. Therefore, our confidence in scaling a player’s quality from a different league into the Scottish Premiership is extremely high.

"We hope to build on the success of the previous decades, domestically and especially in Europe, by helping to build the most talented squad Celtic has ever possessed by finding exciting players from around the globe."

#1822. Crystal Palace v Hull City: Matt Crooks making most of Premier League chance

His career had had its moments by then – he had won at Wembley with Hull City, scored at Old Trafford as Middlesbrough knocked his boyhood club Manchester United out of the FA Cup, pulled on the famous blue shirt of Rangers and even played in Major League Soccer, but he thought the chance to play in the world's best domestic football league had passed him by.

So now he is in it, not just as a bit-part player, but a crucial part of an odds-defying Hull campaign which takes them to bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace on Sunday, Crooks is trying his best to take it all in.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"As a young person, you probably see certain situations and think it's the norm. Maybe you don't appreciate it as much," says the Leeds-born midfielder who made his professional debut for Huddersfield Town.

"As you get older, you go through life experiences and appreciate the highs maybe a little bit more.

"But as well as that, I've got kids and the chance for my kids to see me play and hopefully remember a little bit. They went down to Stamford Bridge and came to the (Manchester) United game (dad's Premier League debut).

Joining Middlesbrough in 2021 was probably Crooks' best chance of getting into the Premier League but when three years with the Teessiders failed to deliver, he moved across the pond, before coming back to join a Hull team in the middle of a Championship relegation fight they would only win on the final day of 2024-25, thanks to his goal at Portsmouth.

"I was, what?, 31 when I came here?" he says. "The club was in a different situation.

"I went away to America and I signed a three-year deal there so I'd almost written off coming back to England at one point.

"But things happen for a reason. Obviously it was never say never. Callum Naismith, who was at Luton, has always said to me, you can do it, he's always been my biggest fan.

"It was surreal that moment (he played in the Premier League for the first time, in August), but now you're in it, it just feels normal.

"The weeks are the same, the games are the same, it's just a lot bigger stage."

Crooks has certainly earnt it, not only with the hard yards put in at Hartlepool United, Accrington Stanley, Scunthorpe United and Northampton Town as well as the club's previously mentioned, but even for delaying surgery on his shoulder so he could first get Hull up via May's play-offs, then make himself available to face the Red Devils on this season's opening day.

"It's still hanging on," he smiles. "I've still not had the operation.

"I can't swim anymore, which I found out in the summer.

"I think I'll get operated on at some point. I think because I'd have to do it in pre-season, I didn't want to waste this opportunity, so I passed up on my opportunity to get operated."

But this is the brutal world of football – there is no guarantee those sacrifices would be rewarded, especially not at a club which signed six central midfielders in the summer. But Crooks and Regan Slater have remained the preferred partnership.

"Do I thank him? I don't know how to respond to that, really," says Crooks sheepishly when the point about coach Sergej Jakirovic's loyalty is put to him.

"The lads that have come in have been great, but the lads who played last season have been really good. The gaffer's going to choose a team he thinks is going to win the game.

"It's up to the lads out on the training field every day to show up.

"Because of the squad, every day we push each other. If you're not doing the hard yards then you're going to get pulled up on it more by the players than anyone. The new lads have bought into that in the work we do on the pitch."

So now he is getting his moment in the sun, how important is it for Crooks to make sure he really enjoys it?

"It's good to enjoy it, but at the same time we're here to do a job, we're here to win games," he replies. "So I think it is hard to catch that balance sometimes. You're always looking to the next thing.

"I think after Wembley (and the Championship play-off final win) I enjoyed it for a bit and then it was, 'Right, I want to get in the team (next season).'

"I think to be successful, that's what you've got to be. You've got to always be looking at the next thing.

"Maybe when the dust has settled and I hang my boots up – it might be sooner rather than later – I can look back and maybe enjoy it a little bit more, but right now I'm trying to get in the team.

"If I'm in the team or if I'm playing, then I want to play well. You're always self-critiquing yourself, I guess, and finding new ways to improve, whether that be in the team and playing or not being in the team and helping your team-mates out.

"You get your times in life and you get the good times and you've got to try and enjoy them, but at the same time don't rest.

Ultimately, though, when those children of his have children of their own, granddad Matt will able to proudly tell them: "I was a Premier League footballer."

#1819. Retaken Ryan Naderi penalty propels Rangers above Celtic as century-old Ibrox curse endures amid drama

The stakes were as clear as the late November chill hanging over Ibrox. In the end, it was not Celtic’s shadow or Falkirk’s fearless ambition that threatened to derail Rangers’ march to the Scottish Premiership summit, but their own capacity for self-inflicted torment.

Yet when the dust settled on an afternoon of excruciating tension in Govan, Derek McInnes’ side had discovered an even more potent trait - an unyielding refusal to crack under pressure, culminating in Ryan Naderi’s retaken 99th-minute penalty to snatch a last-gasp 2-1 victory over the Bairns that sent them top of the table for the first time this season.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

With reigning champions Celtic not in action against Hearts until Sunday, Rangers entered this contest between two of the leagues most in-form sides knowing a victory would lift them above their Old Firm rivals after steadily eroding an imposing deficit down to one point.

Standing in their path, however, was a Falkirk side enjoying a fairytale campaign. Arriving in third place in the table on the back of six consecutive top-flight triumphs, a sequence unmatched by the Bairns since March 1966, John McGlynn’s men had already claimed the scalps of both Celtic and Hearts. McGlynn had spoken pre-match of sowing anxiety on the pitch and letting it spread onto the terracing. For 85 minutes, his players executed that design with exasperating precision.

Having witnessed a stirring second half turnaround against Aberdeen on Tuesday night, McInnes shuffled his starting XI, making five alterations. Findlay Curtis, Tochi Chukwuani, Kim Min-su, Tuur Rommens and Dujon Sterling were all drafted in, while Nicolas Raskin assumed the captaincy in Dan Neil’s absence.

Initially, the refreshed hosts asserted complete control. Naderi glanced an early Tuur Rommens cross narrowly over the bar, and goalkeeper Scott Bain, booked just before the half-hour for continuous time-wasting, was forced into sharp interventions to repel efforts from Rommens and Djeidi Gassama.

However, territorial dominance without a clinical edge carries consequences. In the 33rd minute, during Falkirk’s first purposeful venture into the final third, Scott Tanser’s deep, angled delivery was nodded down by Jacob Murrell. Although Ivor Pandur reacted swiftly to keep out Ethan Ross’s close-range effort, a delayed VAR review revealed Rommens tugging back Murrell’s shirt. Referee Ryan Lee pointed to the spot, and American striker Murrell, continuing a lethal streak of eight goals in his last eight league appearances, dispatched his finish cleanly into the bottom-left corner.

The unease McGlynn had prophesied instantly gripped Ibrox, and Rangers’ frustration deepened after the interval. Curtis saw a deflected strike clip the woodwork, and when he swept home a crisp finish in the 57th minute, celebrations were abruptly extinguished by VAR, which judged the ball to have crept out of play before Naderi robbed a defender in the build-up. Moments later, amid a frantic goalmouth scramble, Raskin somehow ballooned a shot over the top from four yards with the goal gaping.

Sensing greater urgency, McInnes turned to his bench in the 65th minute, introducing Dan Neil, Badredine Bouanani and James Penrice, before throwing on striker Kevin Kelsy shortly afterward. Even so, Falkirk squandered a golden opportunity to extinguish the contest in the 68th minute when Ross slipped substitute CJ Fodrey clean through, only for the forward to falter with solely Pandur to beat.

It proved a catastrophic reprieve. With five minutes of normal time remaining, Bouanani found a pocket of space on the right flank to whip an inviting cross toward the near post, where Kelsy rose to glance a header beyond Bain as the home crowd let out a collective roar of relief.

What followed belonged to the realm of pure theatre. Four minutes into stoppage time, as Naderi headed a corner wide, ref Lee was summoned over again to the pitch side monitor. He penalised former Rangers youth player Connor Allan for an off-the-ball shirt pull on Emmanuel Fernandez. Minutes later Naderi’s stuttered run-up ended in a tame, strike straight at Bain which was smothered comfortably. Loud groans echoed around the stadium, until VAR intervened one final time, ruling that Bain had encroached off his line.

Handed an unexpected lifeline, Naderi banished the collective dread, burying his retaken spot-kick low into the bottom-left corner to spark scenes of unbridled delirium. Falkirk’s 101-year wait for a league triumph at Ibrox, stretching back to November 28, 1925, continues in heart-breaking fashion, while Rangers, now unbeaten in 15 matches, look down on Celtic and others after propelling themselves to the summit in thrilling fashion.

#1818. Leeds United v Coventry City: Daniel Farke looks back on a year of progress – but not a turning point

Most good stories have a plot twist – a sliding doors moment, as the film of that name put it into the English lexicon – where fortunes change. A year ago this weekend is widely seen as Daniel Farke's at Leeds United.

Starting to feel the heat after three straight defeats dropped his team into the Premier League relegation zone for the first time, 2-0 down at half-time Manchester City on November 29, 2025, manager Farke did what his critics said he could not and rethought his tactics. He abandoned the back four which had been an article of faith throughout his managerial career and switched to three central defenders.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds pulled two goals back and although Phil Foden won the game with a late City goal, the course of the club's post-Bielsa history changed. Quite where it will end, supporters are still excitedly waiting to find out.

Had the Premier League season begun that night, Leeds would be eighth with 53 points from 36 matches, two short of a full campaign. They would take that when the real table ends on May 30.

But Farke is not a fan of such clear-cut simplicity, looking on past events not as a turning point, just a reference point.

Crucially, the Whites followed up that Manchester City performance with a home win over then-world champions Chelsea.

Just shy of 12 months on, they welcome Coventry City on Saturday on the back of another milestone win over Chelsea – this one at Stamford Bridge, where they had not won this century, and in a manner they have rarely if ever won anywhere since Marcelo Bielsa watched on from his bucket.

"Hopefully it's not the end of the good period but you never know," chuckles Farke, a man able to make jokes right now.

"We've spoken so much about the Man City game and the change of formation even though we have turned many games after it by playing a four-man (defensive line).

"I wouldn't label us, at least not in possession, a three-man formation any more but the pundits still speak about it. If we're pressing high it's two or three centre-backs but nowadays you get so drawn into, 'Oh, the Man City game, this was the turning point and after it, everything was easy' or we interpret something into the Chelsea game.

"I don't believe there's one big moment that changes it all.

"You have to deliver with hard work on the training pitch and in the games every day.

"It's not just one day that is important for your fate. You create your own fate by hard work."

If they ever make a film of Leeds’ 2025-26, the actor playing Farke will be fretting at his desk, chewing fingernails and pulling his hair but the reality, he insists, was different.

"It was not difficult, not more difficult than other periods," he says of November 2025.

"Working at Leeds United there will always be lots of noise, even after we played the best season in the history of this club with 100 points and winning the title and an open bus tour through the city.

"You have to make sure you win the next game and the next game and the next game.

"I've always handed a club back in a better position, so I've always taken confidence from this.

"If there is then a spell when you have a proper performance but you can't translate it into wins, that's football. You perhaps work a bit more concentrated to steady the ship and turn things around.

"Even at the top level there is always something to improve and pressure when there is noise. So no, I was not overly concerned or doubting myself too much or what we were doing, I was full of belief."

Whilst he is not prepared to read too much into this point last season in that respect, he will in others.

"From a win and the manner of it you can judge a lot from how far we have come,” he argues. “For an away game (at Chelsea) it was such a dominant, front-foot and fully-deserved performance with great team moves. It's not like we are just like a promoted side who has to suffer and play long balls in search of luck.

"We develop more and more into a side who can also be dominant and play even a bit like we did at Championship level. Don't get me wrong, we are not in a position right now to fight for the Premier League title.

"To play the football we are doing right now is something I'm pretty proud of. It describes the path we want to follow."

A year is a long time in football. Who knows what the Leeds narrative will be this time next year?

While the late drama and the opportunity to leapfrog Celtic provided plenty of reasons for celebration, it was the togetherness and character of his players to dig deep when it mattered most to overcome a high-flying Falkirk side that appeared to give McInnes the greatest satisfaction.

“I think there is a resilience, a togetherness,” he declared. “Nobody's playing their own game. Nobody's playing for themselves. Everybody's playing for each other. Falkirk’s six-match winning run came to an agonising end in dramatic circumstances, but manager John McGlynn conceded his side would have been fortunate to take anything from their visit to Ibrox.

“We ended up getting what we deserved,” he said. “I've not actually looked back at the penalties, but we spent the whole second half defending, which was not the plan at all. By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:15

Liverpool have received encouraging news regarding Víctor Munoz after the winger suffered a worrying knee injury against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

Iraola also offered a cautiously optimistic assessment after the match.

"He felt a lot of pain at the moment, but by the end of the match he was feeling better. I hope it's nothing important," the Liverpool coach said.

Although it remains unclear whether Munoz will be fit for this weekend's Merseyside derby, the initial diagnosis is certainly reassuring for Iraola.

The severity of the collision and the sight of the stretcher initially suggested that Liverpool could be facing a significant injury setback, potentially ruling the winger out for an extended period.

Instead, the early tests indicate that the problem may be limited to a heavy blow, although the club will understandably wait for definitive confirmation before making any decisions on his availability.

#1813. Daniel Farke gives verdict on Leeds United loanee Harry Gray's Sheffield Wednesday struggles

The forward is perhaps the most exciting young player at Leeds United, but has found competition for places fierce in a season-long loan with the League One Owls.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Having loaned his much-hyped player to relegated Rotherham United in the second half of last season, one suspects part of Farke is enjoying the fact Gray is having to do things the hard way.

"The reality is it's not easy at League One level to get into the starting line-up," he commented. "This is why we sent him out on loan.

"This experience is important for a young player who is praised so much. At the age of 16 everyone was singing his name, also due to his family bonds.

"Of course it's not easy if you have such an important name in Leeds United's history.

"But this is also an important process you have to go through and by doing this you grow and you develop."

Farke can point to plenty of excellent examples to prove his point.

"I've spoken to Harry several times about this," he said. "For a striker it's a bit more complicated.

"when you look at the top, world-class strikers and when they started to score goals at the top-class level, it's very often in their mid-20s.

"Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or but at Norwich on loan he was sitting on the bench - and older than Harry (he was 19).

"Patrick Bamford started to score goals more or less in his mid-20s.

"Robert Lewandowski was labelled the death of chances when he was playing in the early stages at (Borussia) Dortmund. He went to Bayern Munich in his mid-2s (weeks before turning 26) and won the golden boot more or less every year.

"It's normal for a striker because you have to grow with the physical demands.

"There are very, very rare examples where they score at the age of 19, 20.

"Erling Haaland is one of those examples but he had the advantage to play perhaps for the best team (Red Bull Salzburg) in a weaker league in Austria and he found his confidence there.

"We are at Premier League level, we are playing in England, where you have the best leagues in the world and it's more complicated here to be a striker, the main man. You have to go step by step to do this.

"We could have sent him abroad to a weak league, to the best team in the league, and he could have got chance after chance and scored goals but this is not the reality.

"He has to go through this in order to grow in his personality, to grow as a player.

"He is a player with so much potential and the sky's the limit but these steps are important for his development.

"A bit of a reality check is important but I'm not one per cent concerned about Harry because his potential has not changed and the belief of us as a club in him has not changed one bit.

"You have to go through it and learn to grow by it.

"If you do this, you have more chances to learn at a bigger level but for now it's the first steps."

#1812. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1811. “If there can be a way out” – Moretto states Milan have no intention of offering Tomori a renewal

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a new deal. There are plans to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

As Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

“There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

“Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

“It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”

#1809. Roberto De Zerbi handed crushing Tottenham injury blow as Savio recovery timeline now revealed

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:31

Tottenham Hotspur have suffered another injury setback, with Savio expected to miss several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem against Ipswich Town.

The Brazilian winger had only recently returned from a previous muscle injury before being forced off during last weekend's 2-0 victory in the Premier League.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi now faces the prospect of being without the winger for a significant period during a busy end to 2026.

Savio made his first appearance since the 1-1 draw with Manchester United on October 10th when he came off the bench against the Tractor Boys.

However, his return lasted only around 20 minutes, with the 22-year-old going down inside the opposition penalty area after an impressive run before being helped from the pitch by Tottenham's medical staff.

His exact recovery timeline has not yet been determined, but The Athletic report that he is now expected to miss several weeks. One source has even said Savio could miss all seven of Tottenham's remaining matches in 2026.

De Zerbi confirmed that the winger had suffered a recurrence of the same muscle injury, expressing his frustration at losing an important member of his squad.

"I'm very angry about that, because Savio is a crucial player for us," the Spurs boss said. "It's the same injury, and it is the worst thing from today."

Savio has endured a difficult start to life in north London following his summer move from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £85m. Despite scoring on his debut against Charlton Athletic, he has managed just seven appearances due to fitness problems.

Tottenham already have significant attacking concerns, with Savio joining Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert on the injury list.

The north London outfit were already expected to explore the market for a new striker, but De Zerbi may now need to consider a more versatile forward capable of operating centrally and out wide.

That would help address the lack of options on the left flank, although Savio's absence could also create opportunities for academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old gem scored and assisted on his first Premier League start against Ipswich, offering De Zerbi an encouraging alternative.

However, with several attacking players unavailable and Savio potentially missing the remainder of the year, adding another forward in January would make sense.

Spurs need greater depth across their frontline, and a versatile signing could help address more than one problem at once.

Sean Longstaff, only recently a regular in the side again after about a year with his face pressed against the glass, made the first goal and scored the next two, Dominic Calvert-Lewin lived up to the billing Elland Road gave him as England's No 9, Noah Okafor was electric, Niko Elvedi made the tackle of the match, and Gabriel Gudmundsson produced its best bit of skill.

Big players got rests ahead of Wednesday's game at Manchester City.

What some disrespectfully predicted as a straight-forward game for the hosts turned out to be hard graft for Leeds for 40 minutes, but having finally opened the scoring, they were quickly able to follow it up and turn it that way.

Playing in rainswept conditions, both sides understandably took time to find their rhythm, but it was another unchanged Leeds side who got there first, as Elland Road was in the middle of a minute's applause for Gary Speed.

Gudmundsson carved out a chance for Ethan Ampadu in the 12th minute, but with a deflection on it, his shot went well wide. Jayden Bogle's volley from the subsequent corner went wide too.

Leeds out to have taken the lead in the 18th minute when Ao Tanaka outmuscled Stephen Mfuni in the middle of the field and set Okafor on a run. When the Swiss played the ball out to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, he played it in nicely for a tap-in Okafor did not anticipate.

Bogle's next shot from a corner came off Sidiki Cherif and went for another James Justin almost bundled in. After a couple more, Ampadu leant back on a shot and put it over the crossbar.

Gudmundsson got to the byline in the 36th minute and put over a ball which was cut out at the cost of a corner. From it, Tarik Muharemovic had a shot blocked, as did Okafor on the follow-up.

It arrived in the 40th minute when Milan van Ewik fouled Okafor out wide and Longstaff clipped a ball in that Calvert-Lewin – one of three Leeds players to have their contracts extended this week – got highest to in order to head a proper centre-forward's goal.

One-nil would not have been a comfortable half-time lead but in five minutes later Okafor sent a ball over and when Ampadu made a mess of connecting with it, Longstaff hit a shot which found the net with the aid of a big deflection.

Coventry had offered little the other way, and when they did, the Leeds defenders were on their game.

Elvedi's penalty-area tackle on Cherif after 14 minutes was arguably the highlight of the half, and when Coventry teed up a corner for Gustavo Hamer – a long-time target of Leeds when he was at Sheffield United – to volley from the D. Ampadu was in his face to smother it.

Leeds kept coming after the break, Calvert-Lewin and Okafor producing similar curling shots from the left of the penalty area, the first save, the second wide.

Tanaka laid a lovely pass off to Okafor on the hour, but when the ball came back to him, he shot wide under pressure.

Coming on the back of a quadruple Coventry substitution, the third goal was the most pleasant on the eye of the lot, Gudmundsson producing a quite beautiful 67th-minute backheel for Longstaff to drive into the net, straight in this time.

Although it allowed Longstaff, Okafor and Tanaka to have a rest, Leeds were as unrelenting as the rain.

Calvert-Lewin played a lovely ball to Bogle before taking his leave, but former Hull City goalkeeper Carl Rushworth saved with his feet from the wing-back. Harry Wilson, one of those brought on, shot wide from outside the area.

James Trafford kept his concentration at the other end, making a starjump saved from Brandon Thomas-Asante in the 74th minute.

Lukas Nmecha took the ball around Rushworth without being able to make anything of it and Muharemovic headed over at a corner, but Lampard had suffered enough.
