#1805. Sheffield Wednesday 1 Reading 4: Shambolic Owls provide Dave Challinor with big reality check

His side's defensive performance will have sent a shiver down his spine. It was truly appalling.

After a pretty assertive start of seven points from nine - if not quite getting too many style points just yet - this was a smell-the-coffee afternoon on a cold, miserable, wet November occasion.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His side were all over the place at times against a Reading side whose manager Leam Richardson came into the match under pressure after three straight losses. It was shambolic at times from Wednesday.

Atrocious defending in a first-half spell when the Owls’ backline - minus Liam Cooper - was comprehensively exposed allowed Reading to go 2-0 up ahead of the half-hour mark, courtesy of goals from Daniel Kyerewaa and Andy Rinomhota.

The mood got a tad ugly before a bit of balm fortunately arrived ahead of the break from Louie Barry, who cashed in on some appalling goalkeeping from Joel Pereira to get the hosts back in it.

Wednesday’s awful defending continued on the restart with ex Owls loanee Lewis Wing converting a rebound after Joe Lumley saved his 51st-minute spotkick. Substitute Josh Stokes added a late fourth.

Wednesday made three changes, with Ricardo Santos, Billy Mitchell and top-scorer Jamal Lowe coming in for Cooper, Sil Swinkels and Jaden Heskey, who dropped down to the bench, with Challinor clearly conscious of the club’s schedule.

It was Santos’s first league start in almost two and a half months.

Kyreece Lisbie and Haydon Roberts came in for the Royals.

The hosts made comfortably the better start in the opening 20 minutes with Reading a touch subdued in truth.

Lowe spurned a good early opportunity, attempting to pick out team-mate Davis Keillor-Dunn instead before the lively Callum Slattery found Barry Bannan through on goal in space.

Unfortunately, with his first touch took the ball away from goal and his chip sailed off target.

The charity continued with Keillor-Dunn firing over at the far post when he should have done better. But it was events at the other end which soon came into sharp focus.

Unfathomably, Wednesday then proceeded to go to pieces for a good ten-minute spell to trail 2-0 as Reading broke twice and scored from their first two attacks.

Lisbie was the provider on both occasions.

For the opener, loose play from Santos was seized upon. Wing slotted in Lisbie down the right and with the hosts stretched, his low cross picked out Kyerewaa at the far post for his first league goal of the campaign on 22 minutes.

Seven minutes later, more dreadful defending was exposed when Rinomhota steered a low shot past Lumley after good work by Udoka Malife and Lisbie, with Wednesday all at sea down the right.

It had the potential to get messy and Wednesdayites started to groan.

Jack Marriott - making his 500th career appearance - almost fired in a third and Rinomhota soon should have done so after being presented with the ball on a plate by Lumley, following a wretched pass out.

Fortunately, his goalkeeping counterpart at the other end in Pereira got into the spirit of things with more lamentable footwork to enable Barry to give the hosts a lifeline ahead of the break.

It certainly wasn’t a first half for defences. There were boos from some home punters at the interval - and at the end.

Challinor made a triple change at the break with Kieran Morrison, Jaden Heskey and Liam Palmer coming on for Mitchell, Yan Valery and Lowe.

The switches did not have the desired effect as Wednesday defending went through rough to downright rancid.

Marriott somehow spurned a gilt-edged chance in front of goal, somehow failing to score from point-blank range after Wednesday were again carved open - with Kyerewaa providing the cross.

Another chance then came and went, before another kamikaze moment saw the nerve-shredded hosts concede a penalty when the panicking Di’Shon Bernard felled Marriott.

Wing tucked away the rebound after Lumley guessed right and saved his initial effort.

Home supporters returned to their febrile mood. Reading continued to feast on space as the hosts looked dishevelled and disorganised from a defensive sense.

Cooper, clearly not fully fit, eventually came on to try and impose a touch of order and prevent a bad afternoon becoming a catastrophic one.

Another replacement in Morrison sent a curler narrowly wide as Wednesday hoped to set up a grandstand finish. He then went for glory instead of being selfless and his finish was tame.

Reading should have been out of sight, but weren't quite. Not yet.

That was reaffirmed when Cooper’s header drew a decent reaction save from Pereira in front of the Kop from Bannan’s corner.

Reading need not have worried. Wednesday soon switched off again and substitute Josh Stokes helped himself to a splendid fourth, a neat curler.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Liongola (Gray 66), Bernard, Santos, Valery; Mitchell (Morrison HT), Bannan; Slattery, Barry (Cooper 66), J Lowe (Palmer HT); Keillor-Dunn. Substitutes unused: Trueman, Swinkels.

Reading: Pereira; Goodwin-Malife, Knight, O’Connor, Roberts; Wing, Rinomhota (Savage 88); Lisbie (Reid 93), Earthy (Stokes 77), Kyerewaa (Jones 88); Marriott (Brown 77). Substitutes unused: Stevens, Dorsett.

#1803. Man Utd handed huge January transfer boost as club 'desperate' to sell key Mauricio Pochettino target

By Lewis Blain | 27 Nov 2026 07:57

Manchester United could be handed a significant opportunity to strengthen their attack in January, with one of Mauricio Pochettino’s leading striker targets potentially now available.

AS Monaco are said to be 'desperate' to sell former Arsenal forward Folarin Balogun as they look to balance their books, potentially opening the door for the Red Devils to reignite their interest.

United are expected to prioritise three positions during the winter transfer window, with a new centre-forward, left-back and centre-back reportedly on Pochettino’s wishlist.

Balogun is among the strikers under consideration, with the new Man Utd manager already familiar with the USA international from their time together with the national team. The forward was arguably Pochettino’s star player at the 2026 World Cup.

United could have an opportunity to make their move after journalist Ben Jacobs, speaking to The United Stand, claimed the Ligue 1 side need to sell either Balogun or midfielder Lamine Camara in January to balance their finances.

“Monaco desperately have to sell and will have to lose one of Balogun or Camara in January,” he said.

Balogun came close to joining Everton in the summer, even travelling to Merseyside on deadline day before the proposed transfer collapsed. The Toffees could revisit their interest, although Jacobs suggested the race for his signature could be wide open.

United are also considering other options, including Victor Osimhen and Ivan Toney, but a January move for the former is considered extremely difficult.

Balogun, meanwhile, has scored twice in nine appearances across all competitions since returning from an injury that initially contributed to his failed Everton move.

United's reported transfer budget of less than £50m remains a significant obstacle, particularly with Pochettino also keen to strengthen at left-back and centre-back.

Monaco's willingness to sell could improve United's negotiating position, but it does not necessarily mean Balogun would represent a bargain. The club must also consider whether he is the right option to provide the immediate goals required.

Benjamin Sesko's persistent shin injury and Joshua Zirkzee's uncertain future have increased the need for another centre-forward, but Balogun's return of just two goals in nine games hardly makes him a guaranteed solution.

If Monaco are prepared to accept a relatively modest fee, United should seriously consider the opportunity.

However, with several positions requiring attention and limited funds available, Pochettino cannot afford to spend a significant proportion of his January budget on another forward who arrives with questions over his current form.

It proved the falsest of hopes. Wednesday’s awful defending continued on the restart with ex Owls loanee Lewis Wing converting a rebound after Joe Lumley saved his 51st-minute spot-kick. Substitute Josh Stokes added a late fourth.

Challinor acknowledged afterwards that his side could have lost by several more goals, His side face a tough trip to high-flying Oxford United on Tuesday.

On his side’s performance against Reading, the Owls chief said: "It was really disappointing, quite obviously. Embarrassing..But words are words.

"We'll be judged on actions and what that looks like, so we've got to have a long, hard look at what do they look like as a staff, as a group of players and put something in place really, really quickly to get us through the next period.

"There's no changes we can make personnel-wise (before January), so in the short term there's going to have to be changes in certain games tactically around what we try and do.

"We started the game pretty well. For 15 minutes, we have two big chances, potentially three.

"Because once that happens, our decision-making goes off and our technique in doing simple things goes off. That's not a great recipe.

"You're probably looking at half-time, wanting to get in to try and make some changes.

"We get a bit of a lift in the fact that we get a goal.

"We make three changes at half-time, within three minutes they've had three big chances, straight through the middle of our defence by a complete lack of organisation, understanding and communication. Then it becomes a really difficult afternoon for us.

"Too many (players) in those moments then don't deal with the environment, don't deal with the fact that they play for Sheffield Wednesday. That's something we've got to get miles better at."

Wednesday suffered badly without Liam Cooper.

A pre-match injury doubt, Cooper managed to make his place on the bench and came on midway through the second half - arguably as a damage limitation exercise as much as anything.

Challinor added: "I spoke about it pre-match with the players. Coops being out, we lose a voice. But I see plenty of personality in the dressing room, around the training ground, on the back of a bus after a game and in the dining room.

"I see personality of players and I hear lots of loud voices. I don't hear them same loud voices when we're out there on the pitch.

"That's because they have to come outside the comfort zone and expose themselves and do it in a footballing environment.

"We can't rely on Liam Cooper to play every game, unfortunately. I wish we could."

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A statement from the board of directors said: “We can confirm that, subject to standard legal process completion, Steven Isherwood has resigned as Chairman of the football club, which will include resigning as a director, and the person with significant control, of Haywards Heath Town Football Club.

"As such, the new ownership group will acquire the club, its assets and any known liabilities.

“First and foremost, we want to say thank you to Steve, Jane, Gaz and Ox for their time, effort, and hard work over their many years with the club. We are grateful for everything they have done for Haywards Heath Town and wish them all the very best for the future.

"For clarity, the new ownership group and the directors of the company will be: Nick Draper (newly appointed chairman), Mark Munns, Sean Furminger, Paul Stone, Alex Gathern and Lisa Hardstone.

"It should be noted that assistance and support has been provided by long-term supporters of the club, and returning ground staff, Jeffrey Hammond and Malcolm Newnham.

"This has aided the swift transfer in ownership, and we thank them again for their support. Whilst writing, we can also confirm that Claire Emery has returned as club secretary, which was unanimously voted for by the directors.

"Looking ahead, the new ownership group is already in regular contact with – and has the full backing of – the recently formed working grounds committee, with Laura Watson acting as the chairperson of the grounds committee.

"We have also spoken with Kev Green and his management team, and they have given us their assurances that they remain committed to HHTFC and helping to meet the long term ambitions of the club.

"Our goal now is to not dwell on the past, nor to become involved in any back and forth dialogue regarding what has, or hasn’t, happened previously. Our goal is simply to build on what is already in place, but to also move the club forward. Over the coming months, some of our main priorities will be:

“Sharing the workload: Distributing roles and responsibilities across different people so the club runs as smoothly as possible and without heavy reliance upon a small number.

“Building Relationships: Working closely with and supporting our sponsors, staff, volunteers, fans, players, management teams and everyone else who keeps the club going. We also aim to re-build our relationship with the trustees of the football club, which we hope will be to great benefit of the club, as well as developing a closer relationship with our youth teams.

“Ground Improvements: Getting plans moving for our proposed facility upgrades, including the new 3G pitch and stand installation.

“Connecting with the Community: Being a real part of the local community, starting with men’s first-team training sessions where our youth players can come down, watch, and meet the management team and squad. We will also be attending local events, such as the Haywards Heath Christmas Fair and the Haywards Heath Business Association events. We are actively encouraging mascots for all of our home games too, so please contact us if your child wishes to be a mascot! We are also shortly releasing our own HHTFC app too.

"We understand and appreciate that recent weeks and months may have provided an element of uncertainty for those within the football club. However, we truly believe that this is an exciting time for Haywards Heath Town Football Club. We are looking forward to the hard work continuing, with the aim of taking the club to the next level, both on and off the pitch.

"If anyone has any questions regarding the change in ownership and structure of the club, please contact one of the newly appointed directors who will be happy to discuss this further.

"In the meantime, we look forward to seeing everyone at The HSEnergy Group Stadium.”

#1796. GdS: Bright foundations for the future – Milan, Inter and Juventus’ financial years compared

Last night, a report was published comparing the financials of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter and the findings are very interesting.

The big three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all. Indeed, all three bring in vast amounts of money and have done so for years, which has helped them establish this dominance. However, their records last season show that a change could be on the way.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.

However, the profits – about that – of all three clubs didn’t line up in the same order. Inter recorded a €23m loss, then it was Milan with a €24m loss – largely helped by the summer signings – and Juventus finished last with a €66m loss.

Considering the Nerazzurri’s sporting successes in recent years, it makes sense why revenues are considerably higher, especially when looking at their Champions League records. For example, not being in Europe cost the Diavolo €54m between 2024/25 and 2025/26.

In terms of squad cost, the Biaconeri were uncontested at the top, with a wage of €210m per season. Inter finished just below with €204m per season, whilst the Rossoneri ‘only’ spent €146m. Of course, this is still lucrative.

All in all, the foundations laid at Casa Milan are looking strong and if they can become more successful, their revenues could rocket up.

#1793. Leeds United manager Daniel Farke relieved to avoid post-Chelsea comedown with Coventry City win

Having swept Chelsea aside 4-1 at Stamford Bridge on the back of a home win over Tottenham Hotspur, the Whites were firm favourites to win again at home to newly-promoted Coventry City.

But with a Premier League game at Manchester City in midweek, the danger of taking their eye off the ball and slipping up on a day of unrelenting rain was always there.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds stood firm, and two goals and an assist by Sean Longstaff saw them to a 3-0 win and a third straight Premier League victory for the first time in five years.

"I'm very proud and very happy with my boys, because sometimes you have a standout win – like last season away win at Man United, or just a few days ago at Chelsea – quite often the game afterwards is the most complicated, most difficult one," reflected Farke.

"Everyone is buzzing and excited and dreaming big, and then you think, 'Okay, home game, Eland Road, fully packed, three o'clock on Saturday, newly promoted side, everything's prepared, here we go.'

"These types of games are very complicated very often, and very often you don't use the chance to back it up with three points.

"That's what we did because we were on it, we were focused, we were concentrated against an in-form Coventry side. They had won four out of the last seven games, and you have to be fully focused.

"We didn't have the best start, we needed 15 minutes. I think we had too many mistakes in possession in the first 15 minutes, we had to waste too much energy in the build-up to have this energy at the other end of the pitch, in the opponent's box.

"We missed the first chances and the first moments in and around the box, but we were relentless, stepped up in our concentration, our tidiness on the ball, and had more energy when it really counted.

"And with the top delivery of Sean Longstaff and good header of Dominic (Calvert-Lewin), we opened the scoring and stayed on it, were relentless and scored the second goal before half-time.

"I think it was crucial in the second half to be greedy, to score the next goal, but also to be switched on, not to allow any counter-attacks, any chances for them. This is what we did.

"We could have scored a few more, could have perhaps in the last 15 to 20 minutes kept the ball a bit longer and a bit better to be even a bit more dominant, but overall it was a really good performance, a really mature performance.

"We did what many teams who played Coventry in the last weeks were not capable to do – we were able to open them, to dominate them and to win.

Jayden Bogle picked up a fifth yellow card of the season, and will now be suspended at Manchester City. But even this was not the worst news in the world for Leeds, with Joe Rodon fit and ready to come back into the side.

"It was unnecessary of course to concede the yellow card in this moment, but Jayden is also an aggressive player who takes risks in this game, and also in his pressing," said Farke.

"This sometimes results in a yellow card, and you have to live with it.

"I don't want to change his game, to stop him going into the challenge and trying to win the ball, because then you would rob him of his strength.

"Of course I would like to have him available for Wednesday because he's in really good form and delivers top performances for us in this position, but the yellow card was coming anyway. If I could choose, I would probably choose such a situation, when you have a midweek game, three games within seven days, when you rotate a bit more perhaps anyway.

"We'll find some solution, we always have found solutions and no complaints. It is what it is.

"At least he has time to train a bit more during this week, instead of playing. This helps as well."

Goaded by the Leeds fans thanks to his history as a Chelsea player and manager, and the Derby County manager who knocked the Whites out of the 2019 Championship play-offs under Marcelo Bielsa, Frank Lampard was magnanimous in what he admitted was a deserved defeat.

"We lost to the better team," he acknowledged. "Until the first goal, I was okay with it really. I think the (3-4-2-1) shape (Coventry played to match Leeds') was frustrating for Leeds in giving spaces that we didn't want to give them, which they've been giving teams a lot of problems with, crosses and running through backlines and creating pressure.

"I felt we slowed the game down in a decent way in terms of our defensive shape, but the goals individually are very disappointing for us and obviously critical in turning the feeling of a game and the scoreline going into half-time.

"Maybe today's a little reminder on our journey this year in the Premier League and more important is the reaction and the resilience going into the games coming up."

#1791. Man United vs. Brentford: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League match

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:12, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:15

Manchester United will be aiming to win for just the second time in the Premier League this season when they welcome Brentford to Old Trafford.

The Red Devils, who are 19th in the Premier League table, will enter the match off the back of a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League contest will kick off at 3pm UK time on Saturday.

The match will take place at Man United's home stadium, Old Trafford.

Man United recorded a 2-1 win over Brentford in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign, and the Bees have never triumphed at Old Trafford in the Premier League.

The Premier League contest at Old Trafford will not be available to watch in the UK due to the 3pm blackout rule.

Sky Sports will show highlights on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app on Saturday evening.

UK viewers can also watch the highlights of the game on Match of the Day, which will start at 10:30pm on BBC One and run until 11:30pm.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a disastrous Premier League campaign to date for the 20-time English champions, who were thumped 4-0 at Liverpool last weekend.

The Red Devils are in a genuine relegation battle at this moment in time, and this is shaping up to be another incredibly difficult match against a talented Brentford outfit.

Man United were in Champions League action on Wednesday, and Mauricio Pochettino's side did put in a much-improved performance in a 2-2 draw with Sporting.

The Bees will enter the match off the back of a 4-0 win over Everton, and they currently sit sixth in the table, only one point off fifth-placed Bournemouth.

Brentford are bidding to win at Old Trafford for the first time in the Premier League, but they have triumphed in two of the last three matches between the two sides.

#1789. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Good start to this game. Plenty going on. Arsenal look dangerous and capable of pinning Napoli deep into their own half, but the Italians have threatened on the break. De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Great chance from Arsenal as Eze pulls away at the back post and connects with the ball to send a header into the box. Merino connects with a diving header of his own but it’s straight at Meret and tipped over the bar.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Arsenal being patient on the edge of the box moving the ball around, but eventually it breaks down with Eze losing the ball and then fouling De Bruyne as he tries to break away.

The Napoli players feel that should have been a card.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

The players are lining up around the centre circle, with a minute of silence for the victims of the tragedy in Nepal.

I wrote a little while ago that it was an unpleasantly warm evening in Naples. I now want to revise that comment. It’s nastily hot, and it’s getting worse. The air is thick (27 degrees and 74 per cent humidity, according to my weather app) and I can’t imagine it will be easy for the players.

As the players line up in the tunnel, here are the full teams in black and white:

Napoli starting XI: Meret, Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo, De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour, Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal starting XI: Raya, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Saka, Eze, Gyokeres

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Tzolis, Madueke, Havertz, Calafiori, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman, Salmon

Here’s the TNT team on Arsenal’s left wing, which has been proving very effective so far this season as Calafiori, Tzolis and Hincapié have been finding their rhythm.

"There's really good relationships there"Martin Keown speaks on the effectiveness of Arsenal's left hand side, with Riccardo Calafiori, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapié 🔴🎙️ @ReshminTV | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Vkw1JzATPK

The players are warming up on the pitch, with 15 minutes to go before kick-off.

They are one of four 8pm matches, alongside:

Liverpool vs Atlético Madrid – join Kieran on our live blog here

Let us know how you think this one will go in the comments. Anyone fancying a Gyokeres hat-trick?

Barcelona managed to get five past Feyenoord, with recently departed Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus scoring the last goal minutes after coming on.

First goal for Barcelona 📞Gabriel Jesus bags Barcelona's fifth 🇧🇷 📺 Watch on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/TJmIhMkoXo

Ermedin Demirovic bagged a hat-trick to earn Stuttgart the win over Norwegian Champions League debutants Vikings

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a new leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your official Champions League MD1 Gunners 👊

Good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that…

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

#1788. Barnsley FC booed again as winless run stretched further by “opportunity missed” at AFC Wimbledon

Boss Daniel Stendel believes Barnsley have nobody to blame but themselves after extending their League One winless run to 12 games with a 2-0 defeat against AFC Wimbledon.

The hosts were 1-0 up at half-time after Brighton loanee Freddie Simmonds headed in a Steve Seddon cross from close range.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Things went from bad to worse for the Tykes in the 60th minute when Arley Kay was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity, with Alistair Smith wrapping up the win shortly before full-time.

Stendel understands why fans have become increasingly frustrated by his side’s performances.

“I think today was a big chance against a team that also does not have so much confidence,” he said. “We gave them the chance to score so easily and then did not score, it is our fault, it is nobody else’s fault, it is our fault.

“I said to the players, we can’t start the game saying this, this and this; we have to change it on the pitch.

“They will get our support, they will get our trust, but in the end they have to show it on the pitch.

“I fully understand the reaction [from the fans], I can only say that it is a different club from the one I left, and it is a tough time before I came in and also since I have come in.

“I think the results are really disappointing and they create a lot of disappointment around the club.”

The result leaves the Dons six points clear of the relegation zone, while Barnsley are without a league win since the start of September and rooted to the bottom of the table.

#1787. Will Man City be stripped of Premier League titles? Possible sanctions amid new update before Arsenal showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal take on Manchester City in the standout Premier League fixture this weekend, though it will be played in the backdrop of uncertainty.

While it is first against third and a showdown between last season’s top two, the outcome at the Emirates Stadium may not have too much of an impact on this year’s title race.

This is because Man City head to north London on the back of being handed an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges.

Back in October, City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City, however, have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should Man City’s appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.

Meanwhile, senior figures at some Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport that Man City’s owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for its breaking financial rules.

Below is a breakdown of what sanctions Man City could potentially face if their appeal is unsuccessful.

Expulsion from the Premier League: The most severe sanction could see Man City removed from the Premier League and relegated to the Championship, with any decision subject to the relevant league rules and the outcome of any appeal.

Suspension from Premier League matches: Another potential sanction would be a suspension. The club could potentially be suspended from participating in Premier League fixtures for a specified period.

Liverpool handed new suspension risk ahead of Chelsea clash

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Points deduction: A significant deduction in points could be imposed, either during the current season or in a future campaign.

The size and timing of any deduction would be determined as part of the sanctions process.

Stripping of titles and trophies: Retrospective sporting penalties could also potentially affect honours that were won during the period covered by the charges.

In this scenario, Arsenal would not be awarded a single retrospective Premier League title. This is because the seasons in which they finished runners-up to Man City has not been under investigation. The Gunners would, though get a League Cup after being demolished 3-0 by City in the 2017-18 final at Wembley.

However, no decision has been made to strip City of any titles or trophies.

Transfer restrictions: The club could potentially face restrictions on registering or signing players for one or more transfer windows.

Fines: City could also face substantial financial penalties. The club could be ordered to pay fines, compensation or costs associated with the proceedings.

The sanctions process is separate from the commission’s determination on the charges, meaning City’s punishment remains to be decided.

#1785. Mauricio Pochettino calls up forgotten Manchester United signing to training ahead of home debut

Enzo Kana-Biyik has trained with the Manchester United senior squad ahead of this weekend’s Premier League showdown against Brentford.

Man United welcome the Bees to Old Trafford on Saturday seeking a first league victory since August in what will be Mauricio Pochettino’s home debut as head coach.

The Red Devils go into the game in the relegation zone, but can climb out of the bottom three - albeit potentially temporarily - with victory coupled with Ipswich losing at home to Aston Villa.

Man Utd’s hopes of repeating the result from their last meeting with Brentford have been boosted with Leny Yoro available for selection after his red card against Liverpool was overturned on appeal.

However, captain Bruno Fernandes is a doubt with illness which means he could be absent alongside Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte.

"Yes, we don't know," Pochettino revealed in the pre-match press conference. "He's affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].

"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

With some senior players absence from training on Friday, it allowed for a couple of youngsters to be called up by Pochettino.

This included Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Jim Thwaites and Jaydan Kamason. Though, perhaps the most notable inclusion was that of highly-rated French forward Kana-Biyik.

The 19-year-old joined Man United in July 2025 after the Red Devils had won the race to sign the wonderkid on a free transfer from Le Havre in April of that year.

#1784. Deportivo La Coruna vs. Barcelona: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:20, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:23

Barcelona will continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

Hansi Flick's side are top of the La Liga table on 36 points, three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid, while Deportivo are 12th in the division.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides ahead of their clash this weekend.

Barcelona and Deportivo have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is the former that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to 22, while 20 of their encounters have ended all square.

Lionel Messi is the all-time leading goalscorer in matches between Barcelona and Deportivo, having scored 20 times in this fixture while representing the Catalan giants.

Barcelona have scored 258 times against Deportivo, conceding 112, while they also comfortably lead the La Liga head-to-head 53 victories to Deportivo's 21.

Four of the last five meetings between the two sides have been won by Barcelona, including 4-0 and 4-2 successes during the 2017-18 La Liga campaign.

Deportivo do have a recent victory over Barcelona to their name, having posted a 2-1 win on home soil in March 2017, but they have only beaten Barcelona once since April 2008.

The Blue and Whites have twice enjoyed three-game winning runs against Barcelona throughout history - between October 2000 and October 2001, and then again between November 2002 and October 2003.

#1783. Arsenal selection boost confirmed ahead of Man City showdown after Mikel Arteta update

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta will have his attacking options bolstered for the visit of Manchester City in the Premier League this weekend.

The reigning Premier League champions welcome an out-of-form Man City side to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday afternoon and will be looking to avoid their winless run stretching to three games.

While Arsenal have lead in both games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund in the past week, they have failed to win any of their games since returning from the international break.

Missing from the matchday squad at St James' Park last weekend was Max Dowman as he served the final game of a three-match suspension after being sent-off in the shock Carabao Cup fourth round loss to Fleetwood Town.

The Gunners unsuccessfully appealed for the red card to be overturned, meaning the teenager had to sit out wins over Liverpool and Hull, as well as the 2-2 draw against Newcastle.

Dowman was on the bench against Dortmund but did not come on, though he has now been cleared to feature in domestic matches for Arsenal and is an option as Arteta aims to get his attack firing again.

“When the margin is by one goal, especially with the level of the opponent that we play every three days, how difficult it is; they just need a moment, and it happened with Dortmund,” Arteta said in the pre-match press conference.

“They broke the press after eliminating one of our front players, and they have the capacity to pick out that player, that player has an individual action, and then it’s a goal.

“They didn’t do much more than that, but that was enough to get a point and you have to assume that. But again, overall, if we continue to generate what we’re generating, I’m very positive that things are going to be good.”

In addition to Dowman, David Raya is on course to be available against Man City as Arteta revealed the goalkeeper is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder issue.

#1782. Chelsea: Why Wesley Fofana avoided a red card against Nottingham Forest as Xabi Alonso forced into change

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana found himself at the centre of controversy during the Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest.

With the Blues trailing to an Igor Jesus goal, Fofana gave his team-mates an even bigger mountain to climb early in the second half at the City Ground on Friday night.

After misjudged the bounce of the ball, thus allowing ex-Chelsea striker Liam Delap to latch onto the long ball and advance towards goal, the Frenchman panicked in an attempt to recover and ended up making a rash challenge in the box and conceded a penalty in the process.

Morgan Gibbs-White made no mistake from the spot to double Forest's lead, though Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit three minutes later to give Xabi Alonso's side hope of avoiding a third straight defeat.

Fofana’s additional punishment for the tackle was a yellow card, though there has been some questions asked on social media as to why he was not sent-off.

Ultimately, the Premier League have provided an explanation as to why.

A statement reads: “The referee’s call of penalty to Nottingham Forest and yellow card for Fofana for the challenge on Delap was checked and confirmed by VAR.

“VAR: “It's clearly inside, the main contact is with the leg and upper body. So it’s inside, the penalty’s fine and the yellow card's fine”.”

Alonso reacted immediately to the threat of Fofana being sent-off for two bookable offences by substituting the central defender, replacing him with Levi Colwill who had been dropped in favour of Moises Caicedo starting in central defence.

That introduction did not have the impact the Chelsea boss would have hoped for as Gibbs-White ran off the back of Caicedo to restore Forest’s two-goal lead and leave the visitors staring another defeat in the face.

#1778. Deportivo La Coruna vs Barcelona - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 08:25, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 08:29

Barcelona will bid to post a sixth straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna at Estadio Riazor on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan giants have won four of their last five matches against Deportivo, including a famous 8-0 success in the corresponding game during the 2015-16 campaign.

Deportivo boast a record of three wins, six draws and four defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 15 points leaving them in 12th position in the La Liga table.

The Blue and Whites finished second in last season's Segunda Division table to secure a return to the top flight, and their opening to this campaign has certainly been positive.

Antonio Hidalgo's side will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 defeat to Alaves, but they have picked up four points from their last three games at this level, including a 2-1 success over Osasuna in their last game in front of their own fans on November 2.

Deportivo have picked up nine points from their six home league matches this season, and their last success over Barcelona did come in front of their own fans - a 2-1 win in March 2017.

These two teams have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is Barcelona that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to Deportivo's 22, while 20 of their encounters have finished all square.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League, with the result leaving Hansi Flick's side in fourth spot in the overall table on 12 points.

While the Catalan giants are in an excellent position to secure a spot in the knockout round of the Champions League, they also sit at the top of the La Liga table, picking up 36 points from their 13 matches courtesy of a record of 12 wins and one defeat.

Barcelona are three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid and five clear of third-placed Atletico Madrid, and they posted a 3-2 success over Villarreal in their last league fixture.

The Blaugrana have the best home record in La Liga this season, picking up 18 points from seven matches, while they are comfortably the highest goalscorers in Spain's top flight during the 2026-27 campaign, finding the back of the net on 51 occasions.

Barcelona now have three straight league matches against Deportivo, Atletico Madrid and Celta Vigo before resuming their Champions League campaign against Manchester City on December 8.

Deportivo La Coruna form (all competitions):

Deportivo's squad is in strong shape at the moment in terms of availability, although Bright Ede (hamstring) and Zakaria Eddahchouri (wrist) remain major doubts for the home side.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has scored five times in La Liga this season and is set to continue through the middle despite the fact that he is three games without a goal since returning from a knee injury at the start of November.

Mariano Soriano and Luismi Cruz have both scored twice for Deportivo this season, meanwhile, and the pair are set to continue in the starting side.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal was absent against Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday due to a minor ankle injury, but the Spain international is set to return to the starting side for this weekend's contest.

There will be no Fermin Lopez, though, following the attacker's red card against Villarreal last time out; Roony Bardghji (knee) and Xavi Espart (ankle) are also definitely out of the clash.

However, Rodri and Andreas Christensen both have chances of being back in the squad.

The ankle injury that Alejandro Balde suffered against Sabah is not serious, meanwhile, so the left-back could potentially make the squad.

Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Joao Cancelo, Dani Olmo and Raphinha could also all be brought into the starting team following the European clash with Sabah.

Deportivo La Coruna possible starting lineup:

Roman; Navarro, Noubi, Loureiro, Quagliata; Luismi, Soriano, Casado, Rodriguez, Hernandez; Aubameyang

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Olmo, Gordon; Raphinha

This is a really tough ask for Deportivo against a quality Barcelona outfit - we are backing the hosts to score, but Flick's side should be able to navigate their way to all three points.

#1776. Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Pressure increases on Xabi Alonso after third successive defeat

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea slumped to a third successive Premier League defeat as they went down 3-2 at Nottingham Forest to mount the pressure on boss Xabi Alonso.

Chelsea player ratings: Defender handed 3/10 for ‘critical error’

Why Chelsea star was not shown a red card against Nottingham Forest

Arsenal selection boost confirmed ahead of Man City showdown

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

The Blues were second-best to Forest, who won it through Igor Jesus’ brilliant opener and a Morgan Gibbs-White double after the break.

Emmanuel Emegha scored twice to give the scoreline a different complexion, but that does not mask the overall poor performance.

The latest loss comes after last weekend’s alarming 4-1 defeat to Leeds and Alonso has clear issues to address as they slide down the table.

One of them is Wesley Fofana after the Frenchman was booed and jeered by his own fans after an unauthorised YouTube interview where he appeared to joke about the club’s Carabao Cup exit.

Forest claimed back-to-back home wins after beating Manchester City last time out at the City Ground and this performance was an indication that they are moving in the right direction under Oliver Glasner.

Alonso opted to change his defence after last week’s debacle against Leeds, dropping Levi Colwill and replacing him in the back four with midfielder Moises Caicedo.

The Spaniard did stick with under-fire Fofana, who was booed from the off. Both men came under early pressure as Forest began well.

Liam Delap, desperate to score against the club where his career stalled last season, had a snap-shot in the first minute, but Emiliano Martinez was not troubled.

But the Argentina goalkeeper could do nothing about a sublime Forest opener in the fifth minute. Daniel Munoz drilled in a cross from that right that Jesus sent into the top corner with an acrobatic volley. It was a fine piece of athleticism, even if contact did come off the shin.

That was the only real moment of quality in a first half where Forest were the better side. Alonso’s men had nothing going forward and failed to muster a shot on target.

Things did not improve after the break as Fofana’s night got worse. He lost out on a routine challenge to Delap, who burst clear into the box and was felled by the Frenchman.

Referee Andy Madley pointed to the spot and Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way.

But Chelsea got themselves back into it three minutes later, with their first shot on target, and they needed plenty of luck.

Pedro Neto’s shot hit Jair Cunha and it fell kindly into the path of half-time substitute Emegha, who rifled into the bottom corner.

Fofana was then hooked as he was put out of his mercy, but Chelsea still looked vulnerable.

James McAtee should have done better with his shot after a fine pass by Gibbs-White, while Murillo’s thumping volley from distance brought a good save by Martinez.

Forest restored their two-goal cushion in the 72nd minute as they scored an excellent third.

Xaver Schlager picked up a loose ball, made space with a fine first touch and then found Gibbs-White with an incisive pass, which the England international coolly clipped home.

They appeared to be seeing the match out with ease, but that changed in the 89th minute as Chelsea scored out of nothing.

Neto’s cross found Emegha who headed home to set up a grandstand finish, but Forest held on for a deserved three points.

Yamal has been in incredible form this season, scoring 13 goals and registering 13 assists in 17 appearances for the Catalan club in all competitions.

There will be no Fermin Lopez, though, following the attacker's red card against Villarreal last time out; Roony Bardghji (knee) and Xavi Espart (ankle) are also definitely out of the match.

Rodri and Andreas Christensen both have small chances of being back in the squad, although no risks will be taken ahead of a busy period for the La Liga champions.

The ankle injury that Alejandro Balde suffered against Sabah is not serious, so there is a chance that the Spain international could be available.

There will be changes to the team that started against Sabah; Eric Garcia, Pau Cubarsi, Joao Cancelo, Dani Olmo and Raphinha could all be introduced for the clash with Deportivo.

#1773. Joshua Kimmich blasts Bayern Munich board over Jamal Musiala health situation

Joshua Kimmich has hit out at Bayern Munich’s hierarchy over their comments about Jamal Musiala’s health situation.

Musiala collapsed in two different games in the space of four days during Bayern’s pre-season campaign in the summer and revealed that he had been suffering from ‘absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction’.

The 23-year-old’s start to the season was also disrupted due to a thigh injury and the midfielder has started just one game in the Bundesliga so far.

Last week, Bayern’s supervisory board member, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, suggested that Musiala may be offered a pay cut due to his health situation and claims no club would buy the midfielder ‘under these conditions’.

Earlier this month, Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, also raised questions about Musiala’s contract due to his health issue.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Speaking after Bayern’s 2-1 defeat away to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich described the club’s actions towards Musiala as ‘completely incomprehensible’.

‘Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I completely understand that this isn’t an easy situation for a club either,’ Kimmich said.

‘Of course, I’ve followed Jamal’s journey over the last two years. I mean, he carried us at the European Championship and was our standout player afterwards. Then he extended his contract, got the number 10 shirt here and for the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can say from my own experience, when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it’s not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years. It’s an incentive and a challenge you want to live up to.

‘Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn’t forget that in the last year and a half, I don’t think he’s played four or five games in a row.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So, to a certain extent, it’s understandable that he’s not at that level. And it’s also understandable that the club is worried because of the illness. What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It should never happen that this is played out at the expense of a player.

‘Of course, the club is always the highest priority and is bigger than us as players but still not bigger than the individual. And that is an absolute no-go and not in the spirit of Bayern, especially in the current phase, where I myself have often emphasised how very, very special the club is.

‘Even in my own situation, the club was very, very special. You could really feel that this ‘Mia san mia’ spirit was truly lived. What has happened now should simply never happen. I find it completely incomprehensible.’

Asked if he has spoken with Musiala about the comments from Bayern’s hierarchy, Kimmich said: ‘Honestly, I get the impression that Jamal isn’t aware of everything that’s going on out there. I think that’s actually a good thing.

‘Of course, there was some discussion. For me, the most important thing is that he comes to Sabener Strasse every day and enjoys playing football. That’s the most important thing in his situation.

‘You also mustn’t forget that he had another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury. But I see him and experience him every day. I see how he works, how hard he works. That also adds to the situation. It’s not that he has problems because he’s unprofessional, rather, he’s there every day, naturally wants to get the most out of himself, works very, very hard every day, and I think he enjoys being with us in the team. I hope he feels that we all stand behind him 100 per cent – ​​the team, the management, and the club.’
