#1772. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta reveals conditions for January transfer as Gunners track Antonio Nusa

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has insisted Arsenal are open to a transfer "opportunity" if it presents itself in the January window.

The Gunners sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League but questions remain over the forward options in the squad.

Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were all sold in the summer, with only Christos Tzolis signed to bolster the attack.

Arsenal have scored 17 goals in the league this season, the worst record of the club's currently in the top six, and have been punished for wasteful displays in the last week against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund.

RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa is among the players Arsenal are tracking, but January has historically been a quiet window for the Gunners.

Not since 2023, when Arsenal brought in Jorginho, Leandro Trossard and Jakub Kiwior mid-season, have the club made a January signing.

However, Arteta insisted Arsenal were working hard in all of those windows, even when no business was done, and he is confident the club will be alert to potential deals again this time.

“We've always been very active in the transfer window, especially when we have certain issues," Arteta said.

"Have we managed to get a deal over the line? Sometimes not. So we will see if there is an opportunity there and something that we believe is going to make a difference for the team."

Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke is expected in London next week and he is set to meet with Arteta and the club's hierarchy.

The January window will be one of the items on the agenda, though Arteta was keen to emphasise that the club have already been putting transfer plans in place.

“We don’t wait to talk about these things only when it is face to face," Arteta said of Kroenke's trip to London.

#1771. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1769. How Xabi Alonso decisions backfired to plunge Chelsea further into crisis

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea are embroiled in a crisis. They look like one of the worst teams in the Premier League right now.

That is the reality their highly-regarded manager Xabi Alonso and expensively-assembled squad must accept they find themselves in after Friday night’s grim 3-2 loss to Nottingham Forest, their fourth league defeat in five games.

Alonso and his players must share the responsibility for another incoherent performance from a team that looks so recently cobbled together that watching them makes you feel as though it is August, not three months into the season.

The manager got some selection decisions wrong. Dropping Levi Colwill instead of Wesley Fofana at centre-back was an eyebrow-raiser before kick-off and was punished brutally when Fofana — not exactly having a cracker of a week — was turned inside out by his former team-mate Liam Delap and then fouled him to concede a penalty from Chelsea’s one-goal deficit became two.

Cue a yellow card, Fofana subbed off for Colwill, and Alonso left facing questions.

Similarly alongside Fofana, where Moises Caicedo was shifted back from midfield to centre-back but was error-prone all night and had an off day, much like Chelsea, who are getting used to having those.

Further forward, Danny Welbeck was ineffectual and, if anything, seemed to repel the ball. At half-time he was replaced by Emmanuel Emegha, who scored Chelsea’s only goal at Leeds last Saturday, now went on to net both of their goals at Forest, and will have been left wondering why he had not been picked to start the game even more so than when the teamsheet was first read out to the squad.

Xabi Alonso reacts to Wesley Fofana boos with message to Chelsea fans

Xabi Alonso makes Emmanuel Emegha prediction after Chelsea impact

Arteta reveals conditions for January transfer as Arsenal track Nusa

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

His two goals were striker’s finishes from speculative crosses, goals that just sort of seemed to happen rather than being the product of a flowing move here or a well-formed pattern of play there. Chelsea did none of that, again. Against Sunderland, Leeds and now Forest, they have been confused, confusing and toothless.

In this rotten period where they have so missed the injured striker Joao Pedro and centre-back Maxence Lacroix, they have shown an incredible ability to play people into form. They played Sunderland into form before the international break and now came a gift-wrapped brace for goal-shy Morgan Gibbs-White.

Where Chelsea go from here is really anyone’s guess. Hosting the division’s bottom side Crystal Palace on Wednesday is, on the face of it, a kind fixture. But the last time they faced 20th in the table, they lost at Sunderland and failed to even score.

Most concerning of all for Alonso and his coaching staff will have been how effective Forest’s high-intensity approach to the game proved. A committed press against a confidence-shot defence earned them a victory over Chelsea that future opponents will watch back and surely believe to be repeatable.

That is all their free weeks on the training ground with no European football for disruption has gained them.

This crisis of confidence appears to be teaching their opponents more about Chelsea than it is teaching Chelsea about themselves.

#1768. Valencia vs Osasuna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 09:32, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 09:35

Valencia will aim to post a third straight win in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign at home to Osasuna on Sunday afternoon.

Los Che comfortably lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 46 wins to Osasuna's 21, while 25 of their 92 matches have finished all square.

Valencia boast a record of three wins, three draws and seven defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 17th spot in the La Liga table.

It has been a tricky first third of the league season for Valencia, but there have been signs of life in recent weeks, having won two of their last three in the league and three of their last four in all competitions.

Javier Aguirre's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Rayo Vallecano in La Liga, while they also beat Tavernes 6-0 in the Copa del Rey on November 10.

Valencia, who finished ninth in Spain's top flight last season, actually have the second-worst home record in La Liga this season, securing only two points from seven league games in front of their own supporters.

Los Che are also the joint-second lowest goalscorers in La Liga this term with nine, and that is a concerning record heading towards the winter break in Spain's top flight.

As for Osasuna, a record of four wins, three draws and six defeats from 13 matches has brought them 15 points, which is enough for 13th spot at this stage of proceedings.

Jagoba Arrasate's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Malaga, but they did lose their last away fixture - a 2-1 reverse to Deportivo La Coruna on November 2.

Los Rojillos have struggled on their travels this season, claiming only three points from six matches, suffering five defeats in the process.

Osasuna lost 1-0 to Valencia in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign, and they have only managed to win one of the last five games between the two sides.

That said, Osasuna do have a recent away success against Valencia to their name, having recorded a 2-1 victory at Mestalla in August 2023.

Valencia will welcome Jose Gaya back into their squad this weekend following a suspension, but Sergi Canos, Diego Lopez and Jesus Vazquez are again expected to miss the contest.

Arnaut Danjuma is likely to return to the squad, with the attacker not involved against Rayo Vallecano last time out following the death of his father.

Gaya for Pablo Maffeo could be the only change from the team's last match given the impressive nature of both the performance and the result.

As for Osasuna, Alejandro Catena is out of the game through suspension, with the 32-year-old sent off in the team's home success over Malaga last time out.

Jorge Herrando was back on the bench against Malaga after recovering from an injury and could now be introduced into the starting team here.

Ante Budimir has scored nine times in 13 league appearances this season, and the Croatian will once again lead the Osasuna line in this contest.

However, Abel Bretones, Aitor Fernandez and Rockson Yeboah are still injured.

Dimitrievski; Martinez, Tarrega, Copete, Gaya; Raba, Pepelu, Rodriguez, Rioja; Guerra, Sadiq

Herrera; Rosier, Herrando, Boyomo, Rico; Moncayola, Gomez; Ruben Garcia, Oroz, Barja; Budimir

Valencia have struggled at home this season, while Osasuna have found it difficult on their travels, so we are finding it tough to back either to win with any real confidence.

A stalemate could be on the cards at Mestalla.

#1767. Mauricio Pochettino urged to axe ‘amateurish’ Manchester United star

Mauricio Pochettino has been urged to consider making the first ruthless decision of his Manchester United tenure in the wake of last night’s 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon.

Having trailed at half-time, the Red Devils looked on course for a morale-boosting victory following a quickfire Bruno Fernandes brace.

The United captain equalised from the penalty spot, before scoring an outrageous fluke when an innocuous looking shot hit a divot and flew beyond the grasp of a bamboozled Kaique Pereira.

Any suggestion that fortune had turned for Pochettino’s ailing side, however, was dispelled with 10 minutes remaining when Senne Lammens made his second inexplicable error of the game by dropping a routine cross and gifting Luis Suarez a goal from close range.

The Belgium international was signed 18 months ago Royal Antwerp and initially looked to have solved United’s long-standing goalkeeping issue.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Lammens is now, however, making mistakes at a similar rate to that of his predecessor, the hapless Andre Onana, and Jamie Carragher believes taking the confidence-starved 24-year-old out of the limelight for the spell would represent a sensible course of action for Pochettino.

Delivering his verdict on Lammens’ performance, Carragher said on CBS: ‘You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes ‘an amateur goalkeeper wouldn’t make that mistake’. If that was an amateur goalkeeper you’d be thinking ‘that can’t happen’. That just can’t happen at this level.

‘It is getting to the stage with the goalkeeper now. The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always big if he’s making mistakes. I don’t think the back-up’s even at the level where, no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you change it.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino has the experience Karl Darlow, signed from Leeds United in the summer, to call upon but the new United boss was keen to back Lammens last night following his latest disastrous display.

Pochettino said: ‘That is football. Football is about making mistakes. I always want to support my players. It’s something that happened in that case. I think we need to talk about responsibility and it’s our responsibility too to provide the best tools.

‘I think in this type of action, our defensive line also needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on.

‘Professional players need to refresh concepts, refresh details until that becomes a habit. And I think things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.

‘It’s to blame us because I think we need to manage this type of situation better, because this situation, when you are a keeper, is not easy and you always need help from your teammates. But of course, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve the small details – for sure we will improve.’

#1765. David Raya injury update as expert explains if Arsenal star can play against Man City

Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.

Raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident. The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

There was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright said on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

While Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a big ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That said, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Read our deep dive into Saka’s injury history as the experts tell us if Arsenal have something to really be concerned with.

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

The month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so quickly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he said.

‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’

#1764. ‘Three or four’: Roberto De Zerbi outlines Tottenham transfer plans

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham are “three or four positions” away from completing the squad rebuild.

After securing Premier League survival on the final day of last season, Spurs moved aggressively and decisively in the summer transfer window, twice breaking their transfer record to sign midfielders Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali for a combined £185m.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke signed from Brighton for around £52m, while Savio arrived later in the window from Manchester City for a fee that could reach £85m if all add-ons are met.

Omar Marmoush also swapped City for Spurs, signing on loan with a conditional £60m obligation to buy at the end of the season, while Spurs further bolstered their squad with the free transfers of Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson.

A mammoth summer of spending then came to a close on deadline day when Chelsea pair Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk arrived at Hotspur Way.

Spurs have undergone seismic changes over the last six months and finally appear to be bearing the fruits of their labour and sizeable financial outlay, with De Zerbi’s side winning four of their last five games.

Tottenham XI vs Sunderland: Predicted lineup and confirmed team news

Transfer news LIVE: Paz to Arsenal twist; Man Utd boost; Chelsea shock

Chelsea seal exciting midfielder signing after unexpected transfer twist

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

The club’s position on and off the pitch is a far cry from the dire situation they found themselves in when De Zerbi took charge of his first game away to Sunderland in May, with the club mired in relegation trouble.

A 1-0 defeat that afternoon had Spurs seriously thinking about the possibility of life in the Championship. But as De Zerbi prepares to return to the Stadium of Light for the first time since that near-fateful day, he admits Spurs need just three or four more additions to complete their squad.

“As a team, as a squad, I think we are in a very good position because we, I think we made a great session of the transfer market. We changed ten, twelve players, and we brought all first targets in the window,” De Zerbi said.

“And for the future, I think we don't need in too many positions. I think we need to finish the squad. Yes, in maybe three, four positions, and then we have not to move too many players.

“We need to stay together. We need to improve the connection, the relationships. Improve the style of play, the quality of the play. To improve the mentality, but I think we are in the good way to become better and to do something special for this club.”

Having finished just one point above the relegation zone last season, Spurs have not had to contend with European football this term, allowing De Zerbi precious time on the training pitch to instil his ideas.

They are now, though, approaching a run of nine games in five weeks that will test their squad’s durability and increased depth as injuries continue to hamper them.

Despite their injury issues, De Zerbi believes his squad have an advantage heading into the festive period, with Spurs enjoying more time to rest, recover and prepare for matches in the first few months of the season.

“Yes, I think it is a big advantage,” De Zerbi continued before acknowledging that the benefit of one game per week only works in the first full season when you are trying to build principles and identity.

“For sure, the first season when you are working on the basis of the team, it’s better playing one game per week.

“But if you are from two, three, four seasons already on the bench, I think nothing changed because you have a stronger squad, you have a stronger principle of the play.

“You have not to lose too much time preparing the game or giving information, giving principles. The players in two seasons, they already know everything.

“Yes, you can prepare in the more details the game, more strategy and less principle. While now we are working more in principle and less in the strategy, but at the end it's part of the journey. It's a natural journey.”

#1763. Real Sociedad vs Sevilla - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 10:13, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:16

Two teams enjoying solid campaigns in Spain's top flight thus far will lock horns on Sunday evening, as Real Sociedad welcome Sevilla to Anoeta Stadium.

Real Sociedad just about lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 55 victories to Sevilla's 52, while 35 of their 142 fixtures have finished level.

Real Sociedad will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Europa League, with the result leaving them down in 27th spot in the overall table and out of the knockout round playoffs at this stage of proceedings.

It has been a struggle for Real Sociedad in Europe this season, and they were also beaten 3-2 by Racing de Santander in Spain's top flight last weekend, so the Basque team will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions on Sunday night.

La Real have had a strong campaign in Spain's top flight, with a record of seven wins, one draw and five defeats from 13 matches bringing them 22 points, which is enough for fifth spot in the La Liga table.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side now have three straight league games against Sevilla, Real Madrid and Villarreal before returning to European action at home to Torreense on December 10.

Real Sociedad have been strong at home in the league this season, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat, picking up 13 points from six matches.

Sevilla have won five, drawn four and lost four of their 13 league matches this season, with 19 points leaving them in sixth spot in the table, three points behind fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

The Red and Whites are without a win in their last three La Liga fixtures, though, losing at Getafe at the start of the month before drawing back-to-back games with Alaves and Real Betis.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only actually won one of their last seven league matches, but sitting sixth after 13 games represents a solid start to the campaign.

Sevilla recorded a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad when the two teams last locked horns in May 2026, but the corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 success for the Basque outfit.

Los Nervionenses have picked up eight points from their six away league matches during the 2026-27 campaign courtesy of a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Real Sociedad currently have a number of injury issues, with Yangel Herrera, Alvaro Odriozola, Ander Barrenetxea, Jon Aramburu and Lander Astiazaran on the sidelines.

Head coach Matarazzo will make changes to the side that started against Palace in the Europa League, with Carlos Soler, Orri Oskarsson, Igor Zubeldia, Sergio Gomez and Luka Sucic among those set to return to the team for this match.

Mikel Oyarzabal has only scored three times this season, but the Spain international will continue in the final third of the field for the Basque outfit.

Sevilla will once again be without the services of Marcao, Jose Angel Carmona, Alfon Gonzalez and Miguel Sierra on Sunday due to injury problems.

However, the visitors did not suffer any fresh issues against Real Betis last time out, and given the strength of the performance, it could be a case of same again in terms of team selection.

Isaac Romero and Robbie Ure are both pushing to be included in the final third of the field, but the expectation is that Lucas Stassin will again be given the nod in that area.

Remiro; Fort, Zubeldia, Sarr, Gomez; Sucic, Gorrotxategi, Soler, Guedes; Oyarzabal, Oskarsson

Vlachodimos; Iglesias Sanchez, Castrin, Salas, Suazo; Agoume, Guridi; Vargas, Fofana, Correia; Stassin

Real Sociedad will be aiming to bounce back from a European defeat in this match, and home advantage could see the Basque team shade a close game.

#1759. Xabi Alonso reacts to Wesley Fofana boos with strong message to Chelsea fans

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso has pleaded with fans to support Wesley Fofana after the Chelsea defender had a night to forget against Nottingham Forest.

The Blues defender, who has been singled out for poor performances during the Chelsea’s bad run of form, needed a strong show, having spoken for almost two hours with French YouTuber Zack Nani on a range of topics.

Fofana admitted that he came close to quitting football whilst he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate injury, while also appearing to joke about missing his penalty during last month’s Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool.

He apologised for the interview and Alonso said the matter was closed.

“We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. He has apologised," Alonso told reporters in the pre-match press conference.

“It was not right, he has said it is not going to be repeated, these types of things.”

However, Friday’s Premier League game at the City Ground was a bad one for the Frenchman.

The visiting supporters jeered the Fofana when he was in possession in the first half and a bad night got worse in the early stages of the second half when he brought down Liam Delap for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted to double Forest’s lead.

He was substituted soon after, following chants from travelling Blues fans of “f*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.”

Speaking after the 3-2 loss to Forest, Alonso jumped to the defence of Fofana, insisting now is the time for solidarity as Chelsea aim to arrest a poor run of form.

#1758. Swansea City vs Cardiff City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 10:19, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 11:32

Swansea City square off against Welsh rivals Cardiff City on Sunday looking to remain in the top eight of the Championship table.

Meanwhile, the Bluebirds make the journey across South Wales sitting nine points adrift of their hosts.

With Freyr Alexandersson still deliberating over whether he intends to leave Rosenborg and if that move may be delayed until December, Ashley Williams will remain as interim boss for this game.

The Swansea legend has only accumulated one point from games against West Bromwich Albion and Middlesbrough, yet his side came from behind to earn a share of the spoils versus the Baggies and pushed leaders Boro all the way at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night.

Those 2-2 and 1-2 scorelines versus the fifth and first-placed teams in the division suggest that Williams has had a positive effect on the group after Vitor Matos's surprise switch to Strasbourg.

Nevertheless, this remains a Swansea outfit that have lost five of their last seven Championship fixtures, their only success being a 4-0 victory at home to Blackburn Rovers.

Despite that drop off in form, Swansea remain just eight points off top spot, emphasising that a win in this contest will keep them in contention with the teams above them ahead of Alexandersson's potential arrival.

As for Cardiff, they are reeling from the shock 4-0 defeat at home to struggling Preston North End in midweek.

Not only did the Bluebirds lose their eight-match unbeaten record at the Cardiff City Stadium, they have now conceded 11 goals across their last three home contests.

Brian Barry-Murphy's side now sit just six points above the relegation zone at a time when they are still searching for their first away success since earning promotion back to the second tier.

However, it should be noted that their last two away games have been at Wolverhampton Wanderers and Norwich City, two of three teams in the division that have collected 16 points across their last six matches.

Cardiff travel to Swansea having failed to win any of their last four games at the Swansea.com Stadium, losing three times without scoring before a 1-1 draw on their most recent visit in August 2024.

Having served a one-match ban, Swansea left-back Josh Tymon will return to the starting lineup.

However, Marko Stamenic is still absent through suspension, while Goncalo Franco and Ronald are expected to remain on the sidelines.

Jay Fulton and Zan Vipotnik are pushing for recalls in midfield and attack respectively.

With several defenders sidelined, including Perry Ng who is still having a knee injury assessed, Barry-Murphy may not make any changes to his Cardiff backline.

Nevertheless, David Turnbull, Joel Colwill and Chris Willock are all in contention for returns in midfield and the final third.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Welsh, Cabango, Tymon; Just, Fulton, Eustaquio; Opoku, Vipotnik, Eom

Trott; Kpakio, Fish, Bielik, Bagan; Robertson; Tanner, Moylan, R Colwill, Willock; Salech

While Cardiff are expected to deliver a response to their capitulation to Preston, we cannot ignore that Swansea have been competitive against top teams under Williams's short tenure. Therefore, the Swans get our backing in this fixture, albeit with a winning goal potentially coming during the closing stages.

#1757. Lee Dixon makes Man City Premier League title claim ahead of Arsenal clash

Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.

City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.

Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.

Bubbling away in the background remains the possibility of a huge points deduction after the club were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges for financial breaches.

And Dixon believes that such uncertainty might be playing on the minds of City’s players, telling Metro: ‘Nobody liked Arsenal under George Graham and we built up resilience because of that.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘I think that could have been happening for City at the start of the season with the charges, but that bounce can die off a bit and then all of a sudden, you’ve had a couple of bad results and it gets into your head.’

Arsenal could extend their lead over City to nine points with victory at the Emirates on Sunday, but Dixon believes that it would still be far too early to rule City out of this season’s title race.

‘As a fan, after seeing Arsenal get over the line last season, you now have something to fall back on and I do believe that, from a fan’s perspective, if you see Arsenal beat City on Sunday, you can think that’s it,’ he added.

‘However, as a player, you won’t see any of them coming out and going, “It’s done and dusted”, because City have so much quality. We all know that City could go on a ten-game winning streak, so they’ll always have that opportunity.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At the moment, there’s less pressure for Arsenal at the top from a points perspective and it’s pointing to it being their title to lose, but right now, it’s too early in the season to say it’s over if Arsenal win on Sunday.’

Arsenal have not been at their best since returning from the international break, with a draw against Newcastle last weekend followed up by a stalemate against Borussia Dortmund in midweek.

But Dixon has still been encouraged by some aspects of Arsenal’s football, most notably the performances of Noni Madueke, who has featured more prominently since Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh injury last month.

‘I love his directness because when he comes on, his first touch is generally in the direction of the full-back which is what I hated as a full-back myself,’ Dixon said of Madueke.

‘You know what you’re in for as a full-back coming up against somebody like him. I’ve been very impressed with him but I’ve always been worried by his end product, but he seems to be producing better numbers now.

‘You need to take your hat off to him for that because Saka’s boots are big boots to fill. He’s really had to knuckle down and he’s receiving the benefit of that.’

Lee Dixon was speaking with Metro on behalf of Betfred.

#1756. Mauricio Pochettino’s latest Manchester United deal confirmed after Bruno Fernandes decision

Manchester United have confirmed the latest deal of the Mauricio Pochettino era, with talented youngster Yuel Helafu signing a long-term contract.

Helafu has been with United since signing scholarship forms in 2025, and was a key figure in the side that went all the way to the FA Youth Cup final last season.

As well as being a regular for the U18s, Helafu has made the step up to the U21s, making three appearances in Premier League 2 this season, scoring once and providing an assist.

As reward for his progression, the right-back - who can also operate on the opposite flank - has signed a long-term professional contract at Old Trafford.

A Man United statement reads: "Talented youngster Yuel Helafu has committed his future to Manchester United. The 18-year-old defender has signed a long-term professional contract.

"Everyone at Manchester United is delighted that Yuel has signed a new deal and looks forward to seeing him progress."

This deal comes hot on the heels of Man Utd triggering Bruno Fernandes’ contract extension.

Standard Sport understands that Man Utd have activated their option to extend their captain’s deal by one year, though the club have the January transfer window in mind.

Fernandes’ current terms were due to expire at the end of the current season, meaning he would have been free to reach a pre-contract agreement with any team outside of the Premier League from the start of 2027.

However, to prevent any further distractions, Fernandes’ contract will now run until the summer of 2028 and is expected to return to the negotiation table once the club’s form improves after rejecting two offers.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports. “And there are no negotiations going on.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

#1753. Chelsea: Xabi Alonso facing new dilemma amid Premier League suspension risk for Liverpool clash

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Pedro Neto has provided Xabi Alonso with a major selection dilemma for Chelsea’s next game, with the winger now at risk of missing the Premier League showdown against Liverpool.

The Blues' miserable form continued on Friday night, slumping to a 3-2 defeat away at Nottingham Forest.

An Igor Jesus volley in addition to a brace from Morgan Gibbs-White was enough to inflict a third straight defeat on Chelsea either side of the November international break.

While Emmanuel Emegha twice gave the visitors hope of rescuing at least a point with two goals off the bench, the Blues are now at risk of ending the weekend in the bottom half of the Premier League table.

A further negative from a nightmare trip to the City Ground was the yellow card shown to Neto in the 71st minute.

With that being his fourth booking in the Premier League this season, he is now walking the disciplinary tight-rope ahead of next Wednesday's London derby at home to Crystal Palace.

Rules state that players who pick up five yellow cards in the first 19 matches of the Premier League season are hit with a one-match ban.

For Chelsea, the cut-off point in which suspensions will be handed out for a fifth yellow card is the home game against Newcastle on January 3, 2027. From there, players who are booked 10 times in the first 32 matches of the campaign are suspended for two games.

As a result, if Neto features against Palace and is booked, his punishment will be to sit out the visit of Liverpool to Stamford Bridge next Saturday.

To avoid a one-game Premier League suspension, the Portugal international has to watch his step in upcoming games against Palace, Liverpool, Manchester City, Aston Villa, Coventry, Ipswich and Newcastle.

Neto is already facing one ban in the new year as he will be suspended for the first leg of Portugal’s Nations League quarter-final against the Netherlands after being sent-off in the win over Wales.

#1752. Fulham vs. Bournemouth - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 10:39, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 16:26

Unbeaten in five Premier League matches, Fulham welcome in-form Bournemouth to Craven Cottage for Sunday's matchweek 12 encounter.

While Alvaro Arbeloa's team have struggled for goals during their unbeaten run, the Cherries recorded a 10th consecutive victory on Thursday, with five of those wins coming in the top flight.

After a slow start to life under Arbeloa, Fulham have gradually found their feet under the former Real Madrid boss.

The Cottagers began the 2026-27 season by collecting just two points from a possible 18, although their four opening defeats were all narrow, but the capital club have since turned their form around.

Fulham have collected nine points from an available 15, making the West Londoners one of the division's form sides ahead of this weekend's fixtures.

However, the 15th-placed side remain hampered by two issues: their attacking inefficiency and inability to protect leads, highlighted by Arbeloa's men scoring exactly once in seven consecutive matches and dropping 10 points from winning positions.

Only Brentford (11) have surrendered more points after taking the lead, and addressing both weaknesses could determine whether the improving Cottagers remain in the bottom half or challenge for a top-half finish or European qualification.

Bournemouth, though, have no such concerns heading into Sunday, with Marco Rose's men flying high domestically and in Europe.

Thursday's victory over Celta Vigo preserved their perfect record atop the Europa League standings after five rounds of the eight-match league phase, while their domestic turnaround since a 5-1 hammering at Stamford Bridge has been striking.

After failing to keep a clean sheet in their opening six league matches under the new manager, the Cherries have shut out four of their next five opponents, with a maximum return of 15 points propelling them to fifth in the Premier League table.

While Bournemouth cannot overtake fourth-placed Liverpool this matchweek, they could strengthen their grip on fifth if the teams below them stumble.

Having watched their side win five of the last eight top-flight meetings with Fulham, the travelling supporters will hope for another positive result against the London club to secure a sixth consecutive league victory and an 11th across all competitions.

The hosts' improvement under their Spanish boss, however, suggests that the Dorset-based visitors will encounter stern resistance at Craven Cottage, adding to the intrigue surrounding this weekend's contest.

Fulham have a relatively healthy squad, although Emile Smith Rowe (hip) faces a late assessment before Sunday, Joachim Andersen is likely to miss out and Benjamin Lecomte (Achilles) is sidelined for the season.

Joshua King is the only Fulham player to have scored more than once, with his two goals complemented by strikes from Rodrigo Muniz, Alex Iwobi, Cesar Palacios, Gonzalo Garcia, Oscar Bobb and Ryan Sessegnon.

Bournemouth, meanwhile, owe much of their league position to Evanilson and Marcus Tavernier, whose combined 11 goals account for 61% of their 18 top-flight strikes in 2026-27.

Six-goal Evanilson has also demonstrated his creative threat, registering four assists in 11 appearances, two more than Justin Kluivert.

Like Fulham, the visitors have most of their squad available, although Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) and Alex Toth (thigh) are absent; Julian Araujo faces a late assessment as he targets a return from a thigh problem, while Junior Kroupi will be checked after falling ill before Thursday's comeback victory over Celta.

Leno; Tete, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Muniz

Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Christie; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Fulham's five-match unbeaten run suggests that Bournemouth should expect resistance, but their habit of surrendering leads remains a concern against opponents brimming with confidence.

With Evanilson and Tavernier providing a consistent scoring threat, the Cherries have our backing to exploit the hosts' game-management problems and secure an 11th consecutive victory across all competitions.

Paul Pogba believes Manchester United should follow Arsenal’s blueprint under Mikel Arteta and has accused his former club of living in the past.

United decided to sack Michael Carrick during the international break and have brought in Mauricio Pochettino to deliver an immediate turnaround after a poor start to the season.

Pochettino suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge and that was followed by a 2-2 draw away to Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

United have not won a trophy in their last two seasons and Pochettino’s side are now in an early relegation battle as they sit 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 games.

Pogba, meanwhile, has endorsed Pochettino’s move to Old Trafford but feels United need to look at Arsenal’s return to the top as a model to follow.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he’s a great manager. And I’m sad also for Michael Carrick because I don’t think he had enough time to show and prove himself,’ Pogba told talkSPORT.

‘But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there’s a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win and we all think that they should change manager.

‘The players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere, like Arsenal.

‘But the pressure, I know it’s a big club, it’s Manchester United, was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

‘And that’s all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about them like they are the team that it was back then.

#1747. Udinese vs Fiorentina - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 27 Nov 2026 10:50

Two Serie A strugglers will meet in this week's Sunday lunchtime kickoff, as Udinese and Fiorentina vie for three precious points.

That tally separates the sides after 12 matchdays, with the hosts trailing behind their Viola visitors.

Having sacked Kosta Runjaic after an awful run of seven defeats from eight games, Udinese are still waiting to see an upturn since Paolo Zanetti took charge.

Zanetti started with a loss to relegation rivals Venezia before the international break, then saw his side fight scrap out a 1-1 draw with Bologna when they returned to action last week.

Against one of Serie A's form teams, that was a good result in isolation, but the Friulani still have just one league win so far - against newly promoted Monza, way back at the end of August.

Since then, their season has unravelled completely, and picking up two points from 10 matches has left them stuck inside the drop zone.

Now heading back to Udine, the Bianconeri have already equalled their worst home record at this stage of a top-flight campaign, and they are currently on a run of five straight defeats at Bluenergy Stadium.

Perhaps the only positive omens are that they comfortably won this equivalent fixture last season, and that Fiorentina are also in freefall.

It was a tale of two big home wins when the pair met last term, with the Friuli club responding to a 5-1 loss in Florence by winning 3-0 a few weeks later.

This time, Fiorentina will head north in a similar state of distress to Udinese, having lost once again on Monday night.

Failing to build on a promising draw against Juventus, the Viola sunk to a 3-0 defeat in Monza, leaving them 16th in the Serie A table and just one point above the drop zone.

Making their worst start since 2001, they have now lost seven of their first 12 fixtures and are yet to keep a clean sheet.

In fact, Fiorentina have conceded at least twice in all of the last seven, as Paolo Vanoli struggles to pull off the same salvage job he managed last term.

Vanoli was rehired earlier this season, but after recently sandwiching an away win over Sassuolo with a pair of home draws, Monday's meltdown has sent Fiorentina fans even deeper into despair.

Udinese boss Zanetti is still missing Nicolo Bertola, who recently joined Idrissa Gueye on the sidelines, while last season's top scorer Keinan Davis is a doubt.

The latter has been struggling with an adductor problem, and the Friulani's forwards have only contributed three league goals so far.

At least Nicolo Zaniolo seems to be finding some form, with two in his last three appearances - as many as across the previous 28. Zaniolo once spent a fruitless loan spell at Fiorentina, but he has previously scored twice against the Viola in Serie A.

Meanwhile, the away side have two players on four goals - Argentine pair Mateo Pellegrino and Franco Mastantuono.

They should both feature in the final third, possibly alongside Alieu Njie, who overcame a minor thigh injury to appear from the bench against Monza.

However, Vanoli is still without Fabiano Parisi and Marin Pongracic, while Brazilian defender Viery has just been ruled out for the next month.

Okoye; Abankwah, Palma, Solet; Vojvoda, Karlstrom, Piotrowski, Kamara; Lovric, Ekkelenkamp; Zaniolo

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Ranieri, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Njie

Despite changing coaches, neither side can keep the back door shut, as only Sassuolo have conceded more goals in Serie A.

So, they should both find the net in a tense, scrappy match, which Fiorentina will win thanks to their stronger attack.
