#1746. Exclusive: How Julien Stephan has transformed QPR into promotion contenders

Ex-QPR midfielder Isaac Hayden believes that Julien Stephan has the capabilities to be a Premier League manager one day.

Stephan has QPR in the conversation for promotion from the Championship this term, with his young side currently sitting seventh in the table, having lost just three of their opening 17 league games.

While London rivals West Ham and Millwall have both toiled, QPR have been one of the surprise packages of the season, and Stephan has steadily built a reputation as one of the division's most tactically astute managers.

The Frenchman arrived in west London last season with a fearsome reputation, having helped Rennes to win the 2019 Coupe de France while developing current French internationals Eduardo Camavinga, Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele.

Injuries and inconsistency, though, saw QPR finish 15th in Stephan’s debut campaign, ending up four points closer to the relegation zone than the play-off places.

Hayden spent last season at QPR, rejoining the club on a free transfer before leaving for Leyton Orient in the summer, and he feels their final league position did not tell the full story.

Three Tottenham youngsters who could become the next Williams-Barnett

Man Utd XI vs Brentford: Predicted lineup, team news, Fernandes latest

Xabi Alonso facing new dilemma amid Chelsea suspension risk for Liverpool clash

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

“I think the building blocks were there,” Hayden exclusively tells Standard Sport. “Last season, I think it was up until February, we were in with a real chance at the play-offs.

“We lost a couple on the spin, and it made it quite difficult to come back. But the big thing for me is the strategy behind it all.

“For me, Julien is a top manager. He's one that's capable of managing in the Premier League and especially the top end of the Championship. He's got great pedigree.

“And also the CEO, Christian (Nourry), his strategy, his three-year plan.”

QPR did not invest heavily in a squad wracked by injuries last season. Instead, they found value in the loan and free transfer markets over the summer.

Manchester City loanee Pierce Charles has been a revelation in goal, with QPR boasting the third-best expected goals against rate in the Championship, while free transfers Dennis Cirkin and Boy Kemper have added depth and quality at left-back.

A top manager with great pedigree... he is going to take QPR far

Having seen their promotion ambitions fall apart last season when Rumarn Burrell and Ilias Chair suffered lengthy injuries across December and January, QPR were keen to make their squad more resolute heading into the new campaign.

The combination of increased squad depth, young players coming of age after a period of adaptation and Stephan’s tactical nous has QPR in with a shout of promotion, and Hayden says it is noticeable that they are now better equipped to handle three games in a week.

“I think coming into the Championship was probably a big difference for him (Stephan), compared to managing in France,” he says.

“Playing Saturday, Tuesday, Saturday, or Saturday, Wednesday, Saturday, was quite unique for him.

“Three-game weeks, we always kind of struggled with. But I think when it was week to week, we were always really, really strong.

“But I think this year, he's slightly adapted how he goes about the three-game weeks. There is a little bit more rotation this year compared to last year.”

Stephan, a skilled in-game manager who admitted to Standard Sport last season that he needed to get to grips with the chaos of the Championship, is adapting and, as a result, QPR are evolving into genuine promotion candidates.

Hayden is not surprised that Stephan’s development has coincided with QPR’s rise up the table and says with the 46-year-old at the helm there is no ceiling to their ambitions.

“For me, he was always really open and honest,” he says. “I think as a player, that's all that you can ever want.

“If you knocked on his door and you wanted to have a conversation, he was always open to do so - whether that was talking tactically or talking about how you felt as an individual.

“Tactically, he was very, very good. His training sessions were always really, really good. I think he's going to take QPR far.”

Hayden was speaking to Standard Sport at the EFL’s Power of 72 event at the London Stadium, promoting Leyton Orient’s Joy of Moving initiative - a programme using play-based games to inspire primary school children to get active and develop healthy lifelong habits.

EFL Power of 72 celebrates the positive impact EFL clubs have on their communities and the bond between clubs and local people, with one million people participating in EFL club charity programmes every season.

#1745. Arsenal make approach to sign Spain international to replace £50m star

Arsenal have made contact with the representatives of Sporting CP right-back Ivan Fresneda, according to reports.

Fresneda, who spent time in Real Madrid’s youth set-up, has made 94 appearances in all competitions for Sporting, having signed from Real Valladolid in August 2023.

The right-back made his first appearance for the Spain national team over the October international break, but has just 18 months left on his deal with Sporting.

Arsenal have been long-time admirers of Fresneda, and The Athletic now reports that the Gunners have made contact with the 22-year-old’s representatives ahead of the January transfer window.

Mikel Arteta’s side are well-stocked with options at right-back, with Jurrien Timber and Ben White both impressing so far this season.

However, while Timber is reportedly close to signing an extension on his current contract, Fresneda is seen as a potential successor to 29-year-old White, whose contract runs out in June 2028.

Arsenal are also said to be interested in young Paris Saint-Germain full-back David Boly, although a move for the talented 17-year-old could be difficult to pull off.

Elsewhere, the Gunners could look to strengthen at left wing after letting Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard leave over the summer.

Christos Tzolis made a bright start after arriving from Club Brugge, but the Greek winger has not scored or assisted since returning from injury at the start of November.

#1744. Will Bruno Fernandes play for Manchester United today? Latest update as new hint dropped

Manchester United will be desperately hoping that Bruno Fernandes is able to play against Brentford today.

The Red Devils welcome Keith Andrews’ high-flying Bees to Old Trafford at 3pm GMT in what is new head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge since leaving the United States national team to succeed the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham boss is seeking a first victory in his new role at the third attempt, after a truly chaotic opening week that saw a 4-0 drubbing by arch-rivals Liverpool with 10 men at Anfield quickly followed by an incident-packed and controversial 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting, in which Fernandes scored both goals against his former club.

But the Argentine’s hopes of achieving that have been hit by concerns over the availability of influential captain Fernandes, who has played all but one minute of Pochettino’s first two games at the helm and looked on track to lead the team again from the No10 position against Brentford as usual.

However, reports then emerged on Friday morning that the 32-year-old had not trained at Carrington on the eve of the game as a precautionary measure after feeling unwell.

United swiftly released a statement to confirm that was indeed the case, informing fans: “Bruno Fernandes was absent from the session. The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”

Pochettino then admitted at his pre-match press conference a couple of hours later that he “did not know” if Fernandes would be in contention to face Brentford, following a virus picked up in Portugal.

"He's affected by a virus from Portugal,” Pochettino said. “He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].

"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

It also emerged on Friday that United had triggered their option to automatically extend Fernandes’ contract with the club by a further 12 months, until June 2028.

Fans believe that Fernandes may already have dropped a clear hint as to his potential availability to face Brentford on social media on Friday.

On his official Instagram account, the Portuguese - or his team - posted a match graphic to his Stories that featured an image of him and the title “next match”, before featuring the details of Saturday’s game.

It can be unusual for such graphics to still be posted to official players’ accounts if they are not playing, which can often be a valuable clue as to their involvement when it has generally thought to be in question.

Liverpool have been a good example of this on more than one occasion already this season with regards to the availability of reigning Player of the Season Dominik Szoboszlai during his injury struggles.

However, there is of course the possibility that such a post was scheduled before Fernandes was kept out of training on Friday morning and as such it would obviously have no bearing on his potential availability.

Alan Shearer is back with his latest round of Premier League predictions ahead of another huge weekend of action.

Arsenal host Manchester City on Sunday afternoon with Enzo Maresca’s side title hopes fading after a run of four games without a win.

Manchester United are sat in 19th place and host Brentford at Old Trafford in a huge game for Mauricio Pochettino after his debut in the dugout ended in a 4-0 humiliation at Anfield last Sunday.

Liverpool meanwhile make the short trip over to the Hill Dickinson Stadium for the first Merseyside derby of the season with Everton picking up just one win in their last 10 meetings with their neighbours.

As ever, England legend and Betfair ambassador Alan Shearer has revealed his Premier League predictions to Metro.

What a tough one to call. Big, big game for both clubs. Big game for both managers. We saw Forest when they went up against City, didn’t we? We thought, ‘Okay, maybe this is what we’re about to see in Liam Delap and that performance’. But then it went against them again last weekend.

Chelsea, I don’t know. I haven’t got a clue what’s going to happen because they just got battered into submission by Leeds and that would be the worry. I think this is such a tough one to call. I’m fascinated to see what Chelsea offer, particularly in forward positions again. I’m going to go for a draw. I don’t have any confidence in either. I think that would be a better result for Forest than it would be for Chelsea, so I’m going to go for a draw.

Chelsea are really missing Joao Pedro. He’s a top player. But they were still conceding goals when he was here. I know they were outscoring teams, but they were still conceding. They need him as soon as possible

Palace were a little really poor defensively last week against Coventry, and it doesn’t take a genius to work out what Frank has to do with them. Defensively they’re a mess and they’ve got some of the worst stats in the league. So, he has to stop that.

Sunderland were in Europe on Thursday and it will be interesting to see how much that will impact them at the weekend. It doesn’t look as if Brobbey’s going to be fit again. Obviously, I watched Arsenal last weekend against Newcastle. Napoli, who are struggling in Serie A and in Europe, scraped a draw. I’m going to go for an Arsenal home win. A really, really tight game, but I think Arsenal win.

Maresca is searching for ideas on how to stop them conceding and how to beef them up in midfield and protection. Mark Guehi, he’s having a terrible time defensively. He’s searching for ideas to try and stop that. He left out Fernandez last week to play Anderson, Bouaddi and Foden and he’s searching for ideas to try and halt what’s happening defensively in their team without any look at the moment.

#1742. Aston Villa transfer news: How may Chelsea consider ending Alejandro Garnacho's deflating loan spell?

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 11:08

Chelsea are allegedly yet to determine whether they will consider ending Alejandro Garnacho's loan stint at Aston Villa.

On Tuesday evening, the Argentine was left out of the squad for the Champions League fixture at Galatasaray, despite Unai Emery naming two goalkeepers and having one spare spot on the substitutes' bench.

Emery suggested after the game that he only selected players who he felt were capable of making an impact in that particular match, essentially delivering a clear message to Garnacho.

Garnacho has been restricted to just seven substitute appearances totalling fewer than 100 minutes since making the loan switch to Villa, who can activate a permanent £43m transfer if the winger plays a set number of matches.

However, like in the case of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott in 2025-26, it has become apparent that Emery has given up on a loan player who Villa could sign for big money if they make in the region of eight to 10 appearances.

As per several reports, Villa do not have the option of ending Garnacho's loan during the winter transfer window, nor do Chelsea have a recall clause.

These were the same terms that Villa and Liverpool agreed for Elliott, and subsequently failed to agree over a compromise for the second half of the last campaign.

According to The Athletic, Villa will need to hope that a foreign club expresses an interest in signing Garnacho at the turn of the year.

Garnacho is said to have wanted to leave the Premier League for a European club prior to Emery expressing an interest in his services.

At this point in time, though, it is unclear whether Chelsea would give the green light to a change of clubs for Garnacho.

If it is not beneficial from a financial perspective, they may choose to take no action.

The exact reason why Emery wanted to sign Garnacho is unclear. The fact that the former Manchester United attacker has not made a single start is either reflective of his efforts in training or Emery not having any serious interest in a permanent deal.

Either way, it is clear that Garnacho needs to rebuild his career in Europe, most likely La Liga where he has previously spent time at Atletico Madrid as a youngster.

How that may come about remains to be seen. Any club would likely have to take the bulk of Garnacho's wages and pay a substantial loan fee for it to be worthwhile to Chelsea.

#1741. Manchester United XI vs Brentford: Bruno Fernandes IN - starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest

Bruno Fernandes starts for Manchester United against Brentford in the Premier League today.

The club captain was unable to train at Carrington on Friday morning due to a virus, which threw into doubt his involvement in Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge at Old Trafford.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, and that could have been a huge spanner to throw into the works.

Having opted for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, Pochettino switched to a four-man defence for the chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday, in which Fernandes scored both goals.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, Pochettino looks to have opted for a back four again.

It has been a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available and starts after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game and keeps his place despite having reportedly complained of an injury.

Lisandro Martinez stays at left-back despite Luke Shaw now being back in training. Diogo Dalot gets the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Pochettino has quickly settled on a midfield partnership of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans, who was controversially sent off late on against Sporting but is available in the Premier League.

Amad Diallo - passed fit after a knock - and Patrick Dorgu join Fernandes in the attacking trio behind lone frontman Joshua Zirkzee, with Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo only on the bench.

Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko remain injured, as do midfielders Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte. Pochettino revealed on Friday that Baleba would be out for 10 to 12 weeks from when he first sustained his hamstring issue against Roma in early November.

Man Utd XI vs Brentford: Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Fernandes, Dorgu; Zirkzee

Subs: Darlow, De Ligt, Mazraoui, Shaw, Andrey Santos, Mount, Cunha, Lacey, Mbeumo

Time and date: 3pm GMT on Saturday November 28, 2026

#1739. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

81 - Kobbie Mainoo completed the most passes in Manchester United's 4-0 win over Sabah (81).It was the most by an Englishman for the Red Devils in a UEFA Champions League match since Michael Carrick in February 2014 vs Olympiakos (89).Mentor. pic.twitter.com/59wSvQydOG

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Possession: Manchester United 59%-41% SabahShots: 14-4Shots on target: 5-0Corners: 6-2Touches in opposition box: 35-4

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1738. Opposition insight for Olympiacos-Milan: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to start a Europa League comeback, if you will, in Greece tomorrow against an Olympiacos side who are flying.

From their last trip to Olympiacos, Milan know that getting three points tomorrow night will not be easy. Unfortunately, it comes at a time when they really do need easy points.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In terms of qualifying for the knockout phase, their best hopes are currently finishing in the top 24 and getting through the Round of 16 knockout tie. However, a win on Thursday could open hopes of a top eight finish…

➤ Manager: Imanol Alguacil Barrenetxea ➤ Form (all comps): W-W-D-D-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Hezze, Yaremchuk, Gonzalez – 1 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Freuler, Chiquinho – 1 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

Olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

The spending was almost totally offset by four big sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

In the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey is the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical issues, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

#1737. Nico Paz sends message to Manchester United after transfer interest

Nico Paz is open to joining Manchester United next summer and does not favour a return to Real Madrid, according to reports.

The 22-year-old joined Madrid in 2016 but made only eight first-team appearances before he made the move to Como two years ago.

During his time in Italy, Paz has played a pivotal role in Como’s rise, scoring 25 goals and registering 25 assists in 91 appearances for the Serie A club.

Paz has also delivered several impressive performances in the Champions League this season, including a man-of-the-match display in Como’s 4-1 win over Manchester United.

Earlier this month, reports in Spain claimed that Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to re-sign Paz from Como next summer.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Madrid did have the option to re-sign Paz this year but the midfielder personally requested to stay at Como for another season.

‘I thought this was where I would grow the most. I think I made the right decision and I’m happy I did,’ Paz said in September.

However, The Athletic reports that Paz ‘does not currently favour re-joining Madrid’ and the midfielder has not yet been given any assurances over playing time if he does return.

The report adds that Paz is on United’s shortlist of candidates to replace Bruno Fernandes, whose contract expires next summer but the club have the option to extend it for a further year.

#1736. Bruno Fernandes hands Manchester United boost as Mauricio Pochettino makes huge selection calls

Bruno Fernandes starts for Manchester United against Brentford today in a major boost for Mauricio Pochettino, who has named both Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo on the bench.

Despite starting both of Pochettino’s games in charge so far and scoring twice against former club Sporting in Wednesday night’s chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw in Lisbon, Fernandes had emerged a surprise late doubt to face Brentford on Saturday after missing training at Carrington on Friday morning.

Man Utd released a statement to confirm reports that he had been absent due to illness, telling fans: “The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with the Bees.”

Pochettino later told reporters at his pre-Brentford press conference that he “did not know” if Fernandes would be available for selection as the result of a virus that he picked up in Portugal.

"He's affected by a virus from Portugal,” Pochettino said. “He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and, today, he cannot be part of the training session.

"We'll see. We are going to see during the day and tomorrow, how he wakes up, and we'll see. We're not going to take any risks, because you know when this type of situation happens, you don't feel [you can].

"We are going to pay attention but, still, we decide nothing."

Also on Friday, it was reported that United had activated their option to trigger an automatic one-year contract extension for Fernandes, whose deal - which was previously due to expire in the summer amid further speculation over a move elsewhere - now runs until June 2028.

But Fernandes does start against Brentford, donning the skipper’s armband as usual and joining Patrick Dorgu, Joshua Zirkzee and Amad Diallo in a surprising-looking attack, with the latter passed fit after a knock suffered in midweek.

It means Cunha and Mbeumo are both only substitutes in a huge call by Pochettino, who has made three changes to the side who started the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield in his first game at the helm last weekend after Harry Maguire also shrugged off an issue suffered in Portugal.

He replaces Matthijs de Ligt as Leny Yoro also starts after his early red card on Merseyside was controversially overturned, with Mbeumo and Cunha replaced by Amad and Zirkzee.

#1735. Arsenal vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:24, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 09:37

The stuttering champions and the challengers-in-crisis face off in Sunday's Premier League main event, which sees Arsenal and Manchester City draw swords at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners hold a six-point advantage over Enzo Maresca's men at the summit of the Premier League table, leading some to deduce that another success for the holders could already expel the Sky Blues from the title race.

Out of sight in first place, boasting the best defence in the top flight and taking 16 points from the last 18 on offer in the Premier League, Arsenal have lived up to their early-season expectations as the overwhelming favourites to retain their crown.

Yet, the Emirates faithful cannot shake the feeling that there is still something missing in Mikel Arteta's ranks, after Arsenal's second-half shortcomings were exposed in back-to-back draws with Newcastle United and Borussia Dortmund.

Both stalemates saw the Gunners fail to hold onto and build on one-goal advantages in the first half, before their foes came out all guns blazing after the restart and capitalised on Arsenal's alarming lack of a ruthless attacking touch.

Only four of Arsenal's 30 shots against Dortmund were on target, as their 12-game winning run in home league phase/group stage fixtures came to an end, and their 17 Premier League goals scored so far ranks as the worst among all top-six teams.

However, the holders are five from five at the Emirates Stadium in the top flight - scoring 10 times and conceding just twice in the process - and they are yet to draw a blank at home in any tournament this term.

Interestingly, Arsenal's 10 home goals match Man City's 10 away strikes in the 2026-27 Premier League season, while only Brighton & Hove Albion (26) can better the visitors' overall total of 22.

Such statistics will come as little consolation to travelling fans amid the Sky Blues' sorry slump, though, as Enzo Maresca's men have collected just one point from the last 12 on offer in the top flight after a perfect seven from seven to start the campaign.

The Citizens at least managed to snap their three-game losing sequence in last week's 1-1 draw at home to Fulham - not that such a feat was worth celebrating, though - before they also had to settle for a point in their midweek Champions League clash with Napoli.

Maresca and former Man City players have disagreed over whether the club's guilty verdict and appeal uncertainty over their 115 charges is impacting on-field performances, but the manager himself now finds himself under fire for questionable tactical calls and team selections over the autumnal period.

There is no suggestion that the former Chelsea boss is under any immediate sack pressure, though, despite presiding over a 122-year worst; City are just the second team in English Football League history to win their first seven matches of a season but fail to triumph in any of their next four, after the 1904-05 Sheffield Wednesday crop.

Furthermore, the Sky Blues were swatted aside in August's 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal, who have only lost two of their last nine head-to-heads against Man City and are unbeaten in their last three meetings on Emirates soil.

Fears of a serious shoulder injury to Arsenal number one David Raya have been allayed by Arteta, and at the time of writing, the Spain international has not been officially ruled out of the visit of Man City.

Arsenal will also welcome teenage wonderkid Max Dowman back from a three-game domestic suspension, but Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) and Bukayo Saka (quad) will not be back until just before Christmas at the earliest.

After Christos Tzolis's underwhelming midweek display, expect Eberechi Eze to return to the forward line, where Arteta has a critical choice to make between Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz after the former's thunderous finish in midweek.

Meanwhile, captain Martin Odegaard has another Premier League record in his sights; if he sets up two goals here, he will equal the record for the most assists by a Norwegian player in the competition - his 38 is marginally inferior to Morten Gamst Pedersen's 40.

Man City are expected to head south with a fully-fit squad barring former Arsenal transfer target Antoine Semenyo, who is a few weeks away from returning from a knee injury.

Snubbed from the starting XI against Fulham before saving City's skin against Napoli, Rayan Cherki has surely done enough to hold his spot at the Emirates, while Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye also have cases to come back in after providing assists off the bench last time out.

Goalless in his last three Premier League matches, Erling Haaland could equal his own personal worst for an English top-flight goal drought, having never gone longer than four Premier League games without finding the back of the net.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Guehi, Dias, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

The defensive numbers make for dreadful reading for Man City, who have let in seven goals across their last three away games and are without a clean sheet in 10 fixtures in total.

A profligate Arsenal side may not be the best-placed to capitalise, as only one of their last five wins has been by more than a one-goal margin, but the champions should still demonstrate why they are champions and deal another blow to Man City's already-fading title hopes.

#1734. David Raya injury update as Mikel Arteta reveals latest for Arsenal vs Man City

Mikel Arteta has not ruled out the possibility of David Raya returning for Arsenal’s Premier League showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

Raya was involved in what appeared to be an innocuous coming together with William Osula in the penalty area.

The Spain international was in real distress as he left the pitch, clutching his left arm and using his sleeve as a makeshift sling as he was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

#1733. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in Nico Paz talks; Man Utd twist; Chelsea done deal; Liverpool, Tottenham latest

The January transfer window is edging ever closer as Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham all try to get their business done ahead of time. Arsenal are rumoured to be going “all out” to sign Nico Paz as they make contact with his representatives, while the Gunners are also tracking the likes of Antonio Nusa and made a move for long-term target Ivan Fresneda as they become favourites in the race for Carlos Forbs.

Manchester United are also contenders for Como star Paz but have missed out on Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with Mauricio Pochettino also believed to be targeting defensive trio Calvin Bassey, Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins, plus Maxi Araujo, Alejandro Balde, Rayan Ait-Nouri and Louis Page. Chelsea have agreed to fast-track the signing of Burkina Faso wonderkid Mohamed Zongo amid new developments in the fierce battle for Alex Scott, while PSG want Estevao.

Liverpool also like Scott and are said to be eyeing Lamine Camara and Rayan plus former stars Trent Alexander-Arnold and Jarell Quansah, while they are being linked with Jamal Musiala as Tottenham step up their pursuit of Vangelis Pavlidis. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Paris Saint-Germain are said to be interested in a January deal for Estevao.

The Brazilian is a beloved figure among the Stamford Bridge faithful and made an exciting impact last season, but has found opportunities tough to come by this term under new boss Xabi Alonso.

That has led to speculation that Estevao could seek to leave Chelsea in the New Year, with Barcelona known to hold an interest in his services.

According to journalist Nicolo Schira, reigning European champions PSG also want the 19-year-old.

Arsenal have made contact with the representatives of Ivan Fresneda, according to reports.

The Gunners are said to be looking to improve their depth at right-back as they seek to continue upgrading a Premier League-title winning squad in the transfer windows ahead.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal have reached out to the agents of long-term target Fresneda, who plays for Sporting in Portugal and has only 18 months left to run on a contract that contains an €80m release clause.

The report adds that Arsenal are also interested in signing highly-rated Paris Saint-Germain teenager David Boly.

Arsenal are leading contenders to sign Carlos Forbs, new reports claim.

The Gunners’ interest in the Club Brugge and Portugal winger emerged earlier this week, though it was said that there was no chance of a move happening during the January transfer window.

Instead a departure from Belgium looks more likely next summer, with Football Insider reporting that Arsenal are prepared to “leverage their good relations” with Brugge to secure a deal for Forbs after signing Christos Tzolis for £34m from the same club back in July.

News of a done deal to bring you at Chelsea, who have agreed to sign Mohamed Zongo.

Owners BlueCo had originally agreed last year for the Burkina Faso starlet to head to Strasbourg when he turns 18 in 2027 - with a potential move to Chelsea to follow down the line if he impressed in France.

However, Standard Sport understands that the move to Stamford Bridge was fast-tracked after Zongo impressed during trials in west London.

The midfielder will now be heading straight to Chelsea from Sporting des Tannounyan, having signed pre-contract terms at Cobham after turning 17 on Thursday and posting pictures to Instagram.

As mentioned, Manchester United also appear to be firmly in the race for Nico Paz.

The Athletic reported on Friday that they could pursue a move if captain Bruno Fernandes were to leave Old Trafford next summer, which remains a possibility despite the club triggering their option to extend his contract.

It was said that United held appeal for Paz, who has the same representatives as fellow Argentine Mauricio Pochettino, despite them likely not being his first-choice option.

It sounds unsurprisingly like the crucial factor of Champions League qualification will be decisive in this particular transfer battle, though it is claimed that Paz does not want to return to Real Madrid as things stand, despite their buy-back clause that will stand at €80m next summer.

Arsenal are reportedly making a strong effort to win the transfer battle for Nico Paz.

The Argentine playmaker has become one of the most sought-after players in Europe thanks to his fine form during the stunning rise of Cesc Fabregas’ Como.

Real Madrid have an €80m buy-back clause for the player they sold to the Serie A club originally in 2024, while it was claimed yesterday that Manchester United were contenders in an increasingly crowded race that may also include Liverpool, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain and Tottenham.

However, ESPN Argentina say that Arsenal are seriously stepping up their pursuit of Paz and are in touch with his representatives, having scouted him on several occasions.

Burkina Faso teenager Mohamed Zongo has signed for Chelsea and is set to move to Stamford Bridge when he turns 18 next year, writes Dom Smith.

Owners BlueCo reached an agreement to sign Zongo, then 16, in December 2025 and he was originally due to join the Blues’ French sister club Strasbourg.

But Zongo has now been fast-tracked and signed a contract with Chelsea at their Cobham training ground after turning 17 on Thursday.

Zongo’s current club, Sporting des Tannounyan in Burkina Faso, said that the Chelsea hierarchy decided to change their plans after he impressed during trials.

Manchester United have reportedly activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract.

The influential Red Devils captain was previously set to see his deal at Old Trafford expire in the summer, with speculation that he could depart after previous strong links to Saudi Arabia.

But United always possessed the option to trigger an automatic one-year extension, which they have now done.

Fernandes’ contract is now valid until June 2028, but The Athletic’s David Ornstein reports that such an extension will not necessarily prevent the Portugal playmaker from leaving next summer.

It means that if he does go, then United will at least receive a transfer fee.

Manchester United have a potential ace up their sleeve in transfer talks over Nico Paz.

Argentine star Paz is enjoying a burgeoning reputation across Europe after a remarkable start to the season with Como, which has seen him score six goals from attacking midfield - including two against Man Utd in the Champions League last month.

Paz joined Como in 2024 from Real Madrid in a deal worth around £5million, and it had long been expected that the player would return to the Spanish giants, who hold an €80m (£67m) buy-back clause for Paz.

But The Athletic report that Paz does not currently favour a return to Spain, where he will not be a key player, and is said to be attracted by the prospect of joining Man Utd who need a long-term replacement for captain Bruno Fernandes.

The race for Paz is set to be fierce, but Man Utd will hope they have an advantage over rivals in the form of new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Luka Vuskovic has revealed he chose to leave Tottenham for career stability, admitting that not a single Spurs manager spoke to him during the three years he was on the club’s books.

Spurs wanted Vuskovic to go out on loan again, with De Zerbi unable to offer him a place in the starting lineup, but the youngster was not keen on another season of upheaval and made it clear he wanted a permanent home.

“That (a loan) was their idea, but it was never an option from my side,” Vuskovic said in an interview with the Times. “Because already I have been on three loans and for me, my family, my girlfriend, it’s too much to move, with all the languages, and it gets too much for the person, you know?

“Before they signed everybody, they said they don’t see me at the moment as a starting player.

“Tottenham said they don’t want me at the minute, so I said, ‘OK, I have no problem with that, you gave me a loan already when I was 16, I just want to play somewhere where the club wants me. You can earn from me, so I think it’s fair for both of us.’ ”

#1732. The games Carlos Baleba will miss as Mauricio Pochettino reveals full extent of injury blow

Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year with Mauricio Pochettino revealing the full extent of his injury blow.

Baleba was forced off in the second-half of United’s Champions League clash against Roma on 3 November with a hamstring injury.

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to shoot on goal and appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch.

Baleba has not featured since with Michael Carrick explaining in the days that followed: ‘We don’t know exactly, but it’ll be a number of weeks.

‘It’s definitely not this week and it won’t be any time over the international break. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.’

Carrick has since been replaced by Pochettino at Old Trafford but the Argentine will not get the chance to work with Baleba just yet.

Asked for an update on the Cameroon international, Pochettino revealed he would be sidelined for 10-12 weeks, dating back to when the injury first occurred.

That timescale rules him out of the entire festive period and possibly until the end of January.

#1731. Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Man City: David Raya decision made as Viktor Gyokeres dropped

By Ben Knapton | 27 Nov 2026 11:33, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:43

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is believed to be in with a chance of facing Manchester City in Sunday's Premier League blockbuster at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spain international sustained a serious-looking shoulder injury in last weekend's 2-2 draw with Newcastle United, but his issue is nowhere near as severe as first believed.

Mikel Arteta is yet to rule Raya out of the visit of Man City, and if the Gunners' number one is declared fit enough to participate, he will undoubtedly steal the gloves off of Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Whoever starts in goal for Arsenal should be shielded by the central pairing of Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhaes, as William Saliba is slowly re-integrated, and the full-back duo of Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori, displacing Ben White and Piero Hincapie after the 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League in midweek.

Myles Lewis-Skelly should also make way for Bruno Guimaraes in the double pivot, while the underwhelming Christos Tzolis can expect to lose out to Eberechi Eze on the left flank.

Noni Madueke and Martin Odegaard are safe, though, as the latter chases Morten Gamst Pedersen's record of 40 Premier League assists from a Norwegian player; the Arsenal skipper sits on 38.

Viktor Gyokeres's thunderbolt in midweek has given Arteta a major decision to make up top, but Premier League regular Kai Havertz - who has scored three goals and set up another in his last four matches against Man City - should come back in.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz

#1730. Arsenal XI vs Man City: David Raya injury latest, predicted lineup, confirmed team news for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal will make a late decision on the fitness of David Raya for Manchester City’s trip to north London on Sunday.

The goalkeeper missed Tuesday’s Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund due to a shoulder injury he picked up against Newcastle last weekend.

However, while there were fears that was a significant problem, scans have since showed that Raya avoided serious injury and his spell on the sidelines was not expected to be a lengthy one.

It remains to be seen whether Raya recovers in time to face City in the Premier League on Sunday, with Kepa Arrizabalaga ready to fill in again if required.

“I don’t know,” Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said of Raya’s availability at his pre-match press conference on Friday. “We still have a few hours before the game. We’re just trying to get everybody back.”

Asked whether there was hope that Raya would be available, Arteta added bluntly: “Yes.”

Ezri Konsa appears set to keep his place at centre-back alongside Gabriel, as Arsenal continue to cautiously manage William Saliba’s fitness.

Saliba was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Dortmund but is yet to make a first-team appearance this season. It would be a surprise if he came straight in to face City.

It is expected that Riccardo Calafiori will return to the Arsenal starting lineup on Sunday after being rested in midweek, while Eberechi Eze could well get the nod in front of him on the left wing after impressing at St James’ Park.

Viktor Gyokeres scored against Dortmund but rival Kai Havertz is usually trusted in these biggest games by Arteta.

The German was given a full rest in that draw with Dortmund and he looks set to lead the line against City. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi both remain out with thigh and hamstring injuries respectively.

Predicted Arsenal XI vs Man City (4-2-3-1): Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Havertz

#1729. Chelsea legend John Terry claims £27m Arsenal star is ‘best in the world’

John Terry believes that Arsenal star David Raya is ‘100 per cent’ the best goalkeeper in world football at present.

Raya joined Arsenal on an initial loan deal from Brentford in August 2023 before his move was made permanent for £27 million the following year.

The 31-year-old was an integral part in Arsenal’s success last season, in which the team won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final, where they were beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain.

Raya has continued that form this season to help Arsenal open up a six-point lead at the top of the table after 11 games, and Terry believes the Spaniard is without doubt the world’s best shotstopper.

‘You look at Raya, who they brought in, who knew he was that good?’ Terry said in an interview with Rory Jennings.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘He’s the best keeper in the world, 100 per cent. Catches crosses, dominates his box. Unbelievable with both feet. Really good.’

Terry was also keen to praise the rest of Arsenal’s defence, and believes their current backline could go down as one of the best in Premier League history.

‘I think they’re annoyingly good, and I think if they get to the levels that I think they will and win back-to-back-to-back [titles], I think they have to be in the debate,’ he added.

‘Now, you can argue individually who’s better, this one or that one, but I think if they’ve got titles underneath them, then I think they have to be in the conversation as a collective and individually as well.’

Arsenal will look to showcase their defensive prowess against Manchester City on Sunday to put more distance between themselves and one of their main title rivals.

The aforementioned Raya was absent in midweek against Borussia Dortmund after sustaining a shoulder injury in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle United last weekend, but Arteta did not rule the Spaniard returning to face City.

‘We still have a few hours before the match, and we’re still trying to get all the players fit,’ Arteta said.

Asked if Raya could still play, Arteta added: ‘Yes.’

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali is back in training ahead of Tottenham’s visit to Sunderland, but Savio is expected to spend a significant period on the sidelines after suffering the recurrence of a hamstring injury.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last weekend due to illness, but is set to be available for selection when Roberto De Zerbi’s side travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the previous four games. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Asked if Savio may not play again this year, De Zerbi said: “Yeah, I think [he will miss the Christmas period].

“Unfortunately it’s a tough situation to accept. He’s a new guy and he’s suffering with these new injuries. But this is football, if you see other European clubs they’re all suffering these injuries.”

De Zerbi added: “Now he needs time. He needs hard work with the medical staff. Then in 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know, when he comes back, he will be crucial for us in the last step of the season.”

Savio joins fellow Tottenham wingers Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk on the sidelines, meaning teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut against Ipswich before being handed a new contract, could be in line for more minutes.

Fears over an injury to Omar Marmoush remain despite the forward appearing in training footage posted across Spurs’ social media channels on Thursday. The Egyptian was this week subject of online speculation that he required assessment over a possible knee problem.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo remains a doubt despite returning to training following a calf injury, while Lucas Bergvall will be assessed having suffered from illness this week.

Arsenal have been told they will need to pay in excess of €100 million (£83.5m) to sign Antonio Nusa from RB Leipzig in the January transfer window, according to reports in Germany.

Arsenal are in the market to strengthen Mikel Arteta’s attacking options and Nusa is one of the options on their shortlist.

The 21-year-old, who joined RB Leipzig in a €21m (£17.8m) deal from Club Brugge two years ago, has been one of the German club’s standout performers this season with nine goals and eight assists in 17 games so far.

Arsenal have been monitoring Nusa’s performances in the Bundesliga and the Champions League ahead of the upcoming transfer window.

#1721. Alguacil looks at Milan’s favouritism, respect and playing to win: “Life or death match”

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

For Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

“What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

“We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

“We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”

“Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

“Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

“He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”

#1720. Former Liverpool midfielder Naby Keita takes mental health break

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 12:15

Naby Keita has been out of action for several weeks and is going through a difficult period. The Guinean midfielder, currently at Ferencvaros, has asked the Hungarian club to let him step back so that he can recover mentally, a request accepted by his manager Balazs Borbely.

The former Liverpool player, who has made only four league appearances this season, is expected to resume training with the group in January. In an interview with Flashscore, Borbely explained the difficulties faced by his player, including recurring injuries and a complicated sporting context.

The situation eventually took a mental toll on the player. 'For the moment, however, he does not feel mentally ready to help the team. He has therefore asked the club to give him a little time to put his mental state in order' - Borbely revealed.

The manager clarified that Ferencvaros had accepted his request and that both parties should resume working together in January. Keita had already endured a difficult previous season, marked by several injuries and a complicated relationship with his former manager, the Irishman Robbie Keane.

Having arrived at the Hungarian club in January 2025, initially on loan before signing permanently, the Guinean has failed to regain a regular place in the team. His last start was on 20 September. Since then, he has been a substitute on two occasions, but has mainly been absent from the squad.

Keita's absence comes as Ferencvaros make an excellent start to their Europa League campaign, with four wins in as many matches, including a convincing 2-0 victory over AC Milan.

Above all, Keita's current difficulties are nothing new.

Recurring injuries had already disrupted his time at Liverpool (2018-2023), where he never managed to establish himself as an undisputed starter despite the expectations placed on him after his successful spell at RB Leipzig.

His stay at Werder Bremen then failed to relaunch his career. Physical problems continued to disrupt his consistency, before his relationship with the German club deteriorated. Having arrived at Ferencvaros in January 2025 on loan, then signing permanently a few months later, the Guinean hoped to rediscover continuity in Hungary. But once again, he has not been able to play more than 10 league matches per season so far.

It is to be hoped that this break will allow one of Guinea's greatest talents of the past decade to recharge, professionally and above all personally.
