#1683. Man City injury news: Antoine Semenyo return timeline revealed as Enzo Maresca delivers “good news”

By Oliver Thomas | 27 Nov 2026 14:24

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City attacker Antoine Semenyo.

The 26-year-old has missed each of the last eight matches across all competitions since sustaining a knee injury in City’s 3-2 Premier League win over Ipswich Town on October 17.

Semenyo was initially ruled out for eight weeks by Maresca, with a return in mid-to-late December deemed a realistic target for the Ghana international.

However, Maresca has now suggested that Semenyo could make a first-team comeback for Man City sooner than anticipated.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday ahead of Man City’s trip to Arsenal on Sunday, Maresca said: "We have good news. Semenyo is quite close [to returning]. That is good news for us!

“But the rest, they are all OK... [Semenyo] is already on the pitch, he is very close. Hopefully he can be [back] probably next week. We hope so.”

It remains to be seen whether Semenyo will be back as early as next Wednesday when Man City host Leeds United in the Premier League, but he could instead feature in some capacity away against Brentford on December 5.

Discussing whether Semenyo has been missed, Maresca added: "I was laughing with him yesterday; I told him that in the Premier League the last game we won was with him inside the pitch. So I told him, 'We need you back soon to win games’.

"I think Antoine is an important player, but we have more players that are playing in his position and doing well, like Iliman [Ndiaye] in this moment, but he needs time to recover."

Man City have won three, drawn two and lost three of their last eight games without Semenyo in all competitions, scoring no goals or just one goal in four of those matches.

The Citizens have once again been heavily reliant on Erling Haaland’s goals this season, but even he has endured a recent blip, failing to make the net ripple in four of his last five matches in all tournaments.

Rayan Cherki has stepped up with two goals in his last three appearances, but Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye – two wide options who compete with Semenyo for starts when everyone is fit – have scored just one goal between them all season.

That is one reason why Semenyo’s imminent return will provide a vital spark for Maresca’s side, who won all seven Premier League matches he featured in before his injury.

Prior to being sidelined in mid-October, Semenyo was averaging a goal involvement every 111 minutes in the top flight with two goals and three assists in seven appearances.

Having already registered 13 goals in 37 appearances  since arriving from Bournemouth in January – including nine goals and four assists in 24 Premier League outings – his directness and proven end product would help ease the scoring burden on Haaland.

#1682. Barcelona pressure a privilege, says Flick

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick is embracing the pressure of some huge upcoming games for Barcelona.

Barca, who hold a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga heading into MD14, face Deportivo A Coruna on Sunday.

They then take on Atletico Madrid, Celta Vigo, Manchester City, Malaga and Barcelona before the winter break.

But Flick is full of confidence in the two-time reigning LaLiga champions.

"When I signed the contract here at Barca, I already knew what was coming," Flick said.

"I have the feeling that the players know it's a privilege to be at Barca. In a player's career, it's the most important thing.

"The pressure is high, but when you win titles, the emotion is immense. We want to recapture the feeling we had in the last two years with the [title] parades, when we made our fans happy."

Barca have scored 51 goals in LaLiga 2026-27, the second-best goalscoring record by a team after their first 13 games of a season in the competition, after Athletic Club in 1930-31 (60).

They are also well set in the Champions League, having won four of their five games, losing only to holders Paris Saint-Germain.

Barca dispatched Sabah 4-1 on Wednesday, but Flick explained why he was not totally happy with the Blaugrana's display in Baku.

"We controlled the game, but there was a mistake at the end, just like at the start of the match against Villarreal [last week]," he said.

"We're working on making fewer mistakes. I was angry; I was going to kick the ball, but I could have gotten a red card, so I kicked it backwards.

"I like the team to be focused. You have to respect all your opponents. But the objective was to win, and we did. I was angry because I would have preferred to win 4-0, not 4-1."

Deportivo A Coruna – Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang

Aubameyang is only the second player to score for both Deportivo (five goals in 10 games) and Barcelona (11 in 18) in LaLiga in the 21st century, after Isaac Cuenca (two goals for each side).

However, he comes into this game on the back of his involvement in a car crash earlier this week, though he came out unscathed.

"It was a bit of a scare, but in the end we're all right, that's the most important thing," he said. "These things happen in life; for me, the most important thing is also that the person who was involved in the collision with me is unharmed too. After bad things, good things always follow."

Yamal missed the match against Sabah, but Flick confirmed the teenager will be available.

The Spain star has provided nine assists in LaLiga this season, more than any other player in the big five European leagues this term.

Only Angel Di María in 2011-12 (10) has provided more assists after his club's first 13 games of a single campaign in the competition in the 21st century.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 28, 2026

Barca have won their six away games in LaLiga in the 2026-27 season and could win their first seven away games in a single season in the competition for the third time in their history, after the 2010-11 and 2012-13 campaigns, in which they won their first 10.

Deportivo, who sit 12th in LaLiga, have made six errors leading to a goal, more than any other team and the highest tally by a side after their first 13 games of a season in the competition since Granada in 2014-15 (eight).

However, Deportivo are unbeaten in their last three home games in LaLiga (W1 D2), winning the last one (2-1 vs Osasuna). The last time they recorded two consecutive home wins in the competition was in September 2017 (W2).

But Barca have scored in each of their last 10 LaLiga matches against Deportivo (36 goals) and, should they score at the Estadio Abanca-Riazor, they will set their best scoring run against them in the competition's history (11 games).

Deportivo have won just two of their 25 LaLiga matches against Barcelona since January 2004 (D6 L17), after winning nine of their previous 12 encounters in the competition (L3).

And Barca have won six of their last seven away LaLiga games against Deportivo (L1), twice as many victories as they managed in their previous 17 visits to them in the competition (W3 D4 L10).

#1681. Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday

The Istanbul Governor's Office said 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive

Reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’

Villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

To invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

#1679. Leeds United news: Whites confirm extension for Ao Tanaka with contract length revealed

By Carter White | 27 Nov 2026 14:30

Leeds United have announced a contract extension for midfielder Ao Tanaka until the summer of 2029 .

Daniel Farke's side have made an excellent start to the top-flight campaign with the Japanese maestro in the XI, with the Elland Road club currently occupying seventh position in the Premier League standings.

It was reported earlier this week that Leeds were closing in on an agreement with Tanaka, who has played 90 times for the Yorkshire giants since a permanent move from Fortuna Dusseldorf in August 2024.

In that time, the 28-year-old has helped Farke's men secure promotion from the Championship, sealing the second-tier title on the final day of the 2024-25 campaign on the road at Plymouth Argyle.

Last campaign, Tanaka featured 28 times in the Premier League as the Whites comfortably avoided a relegation battle, with the aim now to push on and qualify for European competition in the near future.

✍️ ?? ??????? ??? ???? ?? ?????? ???? Leeds United are thrilled to announce midfielder Ao Tanaka has signed a new contract and will remain at the club until 2029. https://t.co/WuCgHJZ7Wj

Posting to their official social media accounts on Friday morning (November 27), Leeds initially teased a major piece of squad news, before fully revealing the exciting update regarding Tanaka.

The Elland Road club have announced that the 28-year-old has put pen to paper on a contract extension at the Premier League club, committing him to the cause until the conclusion of the 2028-29 term.

Joining Leeds in the summer of 2024, Tanaka's previous contract was set to expire in June 2028, meaning that the midfielder has another year of security within the ranks of the football club.

There were real question marks over whether the Japanese player would make it past the recent summer transfer window with the Whites following a difficult 2025-26 term on a personal note.

After the first half of the season, Tanaka had fallen down the pecking order of head coach Farke, and it was not crazy to suggest that the midfielder might have been out of the door during the off-season.

Starting nine top-flight matches so far this season, Tanaka has cemented himself into the starting XI of Leeds in the league - a feat that he did not manage during large portions of last term.

Tanaka is set to play from the beginning once again on Saturday afternoon, when the Whites welcome recently-promoted Coventry to Elland Road for the first time since a Championship contest September 2024.

Another winnable-looking home fixture against Ipswich Town arrives next weekend, but in between Farke's troops make the trip to the base of Manchester City on December 2.

#1678. Sevilla boss Garcia: Real Sociedad may be ‘best of the rest’ in Spain

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia believes Real Sociedad have a case to be the best of the rest in LaLiga, arguing Sunday's showdown at the Anoeta will be one of the toughest tests awaiting his side.

Just three points separate La Real and Sevilla after 13 games, with the hosts sitting fifth in LaLiga and their visitors nestled in seventh ahead of the weekend's action.

Sevilla's impressive start to the season has come as something of a surprise after they found themselves scrapping for survival in 2025-26, with Garcia earning plaudits for his work on a tight budget.

La Real, meanwhile, were beaten 2-1 by Crystal Palace in the Europa League on Thursday, having also lost 3-2 at Racing Santander in their previous game in LaLiga.

But given the sheer amount of star power available to Pellegrino Matarazzo in the opposing dugout, Garcia knows Sevilla will need to be at their best.

"For me, they are a very good side, destined to finish in the top six or seven," Garcia said of Sevilla's upcoming opponents.

"They've got a lot of quality, plenty of depth in their squad and can compete in two competitions at once.

"[Against Crystal Palace], right up until the sending-off, they were playing a brilliant game. Then they were reduced to 10 men and that affected the result, but they're one of the toughest opponents, after the big three.

"There are two or three teams we all know will be up there, and they are one of them. They have plenty of individual quality, players who can decide matches on their own.

"Against opponents like this, if you're not at your best and not on form, it really shows. They have quality, not just in the starting XI but on the bench too. It's a very well-rounded squad."

𝐓𝐎𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐑𝐎𝐖: #RealSociedadSevilla  https://t.co/f0ikpBlae1

— Sevilla FC (@SevillaFC_ENG) November 28, 2026

Real Sociedad were well on top against Palace in their midweek European fixture, until Jon Martin was sent off and conceded the first of two penalties in the 71st minute.

And Matarazzo wants his side to keep calm and continue playing their way, saying: "We are very calm about the last two matches.

"As I said, you have to differentiate between the performances and the results. We can influence the performances and keep pushing to the limit.

"We are very calm and hope to give a great performance tomorrow against Sevilla, because we need it.

"They are a very good team who know how to compete very hard, and we will need that level of competitiveness tomorrow."

Squad list for tomorrow’s clash. https://t.co/gwVHu1FxJU

— Real Sociedad   (@RealSociedadEN) November 28, 2026

World Cup-winning forward Oyarzabal has scored six goals in 19 LaLiga appearances against Sevilla, including three goals in his last four games against them in the competition.

Oyarzabal has recorded three goals and two assists in LaLiga so far this term.

Salas comes into this game in great form after netting in two of his last three LaLiga matches, as many goals as he managed in his previous 37 outings in the competition.

La Real have lost three of their last five LaLiga matches against Sevilla (W2) after not losing any of their previous five against them in the competition (W3 D2).

However, Sevilla have lost on three of their last four visits to the Anoeta in LaLiga, after picking up points on each of their previous four trips (W1 D3).

They are on their longest run of games with a goal at the Anoeta since 1956, though, scoring on each of their last four trips (four goals in total, the run ending in 1956 saw 11 goals in six visits).

La Real have lost two of their last three matches in LaLiga (W1), after winning six of their previous eight (D1 L1), though Sevilla have also been off the mark lately.

Sunday's visitors have failed to win any of their last three games in LaLiga (D2 L1), drawing their last two. They have not played out more consecutive draws in the competition since a five-match streak in November 2023.

#1677. Inzaghi recalls beating Liverpool in Athens and ’emotional’ affection from Milan fans

In the hearts and minds of AC Milan fans around the world, Pippo Inzaghi’s name is inseparably linked to Athens.

Inzaghi gave Milan their seventh Champions League title on 23 May 2007 in the Greek capital with a brace that swept Liverpool aside. The first goal was an Andrea Pirlo free-kick that he deflected in, the second an assist from Kaka that he rounded Pepe Reina from and slotted in.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was he who allowed the Rossoneri to take their long-awaited and long-desired revenge on the Reds after the Istanbul defeat two years earlier. That feat – at the Spyros Louis Olympic Stadium and not at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium – has remained in the minds of all Milan fans.

It is the most recent of the Champions League titles raised to the sky, and while Inzaghi’s mind is on finishing the job with Palermo (top of Serie B), he will watch his old side on TV tonight. The former striker spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Dor you and for Milan, thinking back to Athens is never trivial…

“Absolutely. In Athens I experienced one of the most important nights of my career, so it’s a city I associate with special memories and that’s why it will always remain close to my heart.”

Tell us three memories from that game. Let’s start with a pre-match one…

“The anticipation of the match: I knew how important that final was and I felt it could be a special evening.”

“The highlight was, of course, the second goal. A moment later, I realised the cup was really close.”

“After that final, I didn’t sleep for ten days. I woke up in the middle of the night thinking that victory with my goals had been a dream.”

Given what that cup represented, that is, the famous ‘after Istanbul, there’s always Athens’ that was printed on the back of AC Milan’s second shirt this season, is the 2006-07 Champions League a joy comparable to Italy’s World Cup victory in Berlin a few months earlier?

“They’re two different memories because they’ve both enriched my footballing life. Winning the World Cup is the ultimate accolade for any footballer.

“Athens, however, also had a special meaning for Milan’s history: we were coming off a disappointment that I’d experienced from the outside, from the stands [he was injured] and I could finally be on the pitch to contribute to the victory.

“Fate gave me a second chance, and it went as you all know… However, I wouldn’t rank the two nights of glory because I carry them with me in different ways.”

Before Milan-Atalanta, when you came to San Siro, you understood from the huge applause and chants how much the Rossoneri fans still love you and you said: “Every time I come back here it’s like it’s the first time.”

“Returning to San Siro and feeling that affection was truly emotional for me, especially because it was the first time for my son Edoardo, who is now five years old.”

What does it mean to you, years after leaving AC Milan as a player and the 2014-15 season in which you were the coach, to still be so loved by the fans?

“I spent extraordinary years at Milan: the bond with the fans was born from goals, victories, but also from the commitment I always tried to put in. Knowing that all this has gone down in history is a priceless gift.”

What do you hope for Milan on their return to Athens tonight, needing a win given their position in the Europa League table?

“I hope we can face the match with character and return home having experienced a great European night. I know how much that shirt means and how much the fans expect from a match like this. I hope the team can give them joy and a victory.”

#1676. Man United make 'major' decision on Bruno Fernandes' future at Old Trafford amid exit talk

By Matt Law | 27 Nov 2026 14:31, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 14:32

Manchester United have reportedly activated an option to extend the contract of captain Bruno Fernandes until the summer of 2028.

Fernandes' current deal had been due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 campaign, meaning that foreign clubs would have been free to agree a contract with the Portugal international in January.

Man United are working to sign their captain to a new long-term deal, but discussions have been placed on hold amid the team's struggles.

Fernandes said ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon that his current focus was on helping the club navigate their way through an incredibly difficult period.

"For us to start winning games and then we can talk about contract," Fernandes told reporters when asked what would need to happen for him to sign a new deal.

"It’s not important now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that. The conversations stopped when we thought now was not the moment."

However, according to The Athletic, Man United have now activated their one-year option, meaning that the attacker's deal now runs until the summer of 2028.

An excellent 2025-26 campaign saw Fernandes earn the FWA Footballer of the Year and PFA Player of the Year awards, with the 32-year-old breaking the Premier League assist record to register 21 in a single season.

There has been criticism of the attacker's form this season, but he has still come up with eight goals and three assists in 16 appearances in all competitions.

Fernandes has four goals and two assists in 10 Premier League appearances this season, while he struck twice against Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday to make it four goals and one assist in five appearances in the competition this term.

The Red Devils captain had been in line to make his 11th Premier League appearance of the season against Brentford on Saturday afternoon, but he has now emerged as a major doubt for that match due to an illness.

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino said during Friday's press conference that a final decision on Fernandes' involvement would not be made until Saturday morning.

There remains speculation surrounding Fernandes' long-term future at Old Trafford, with Man United thought to be putting plans in place in the event that the Portuguese leaves at the end of the season; Como's Nico Paz is said to be a genuine option for the Red Devils.

Fernandes will go down as one of Man United's best-ever signings considering his output, scoring 115 goals and registering 111 assists in 343 appearances for the Red Devils since arriving from Sporting in January 2020.

#1675. Crystal Palace vs. Hull City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 16:26

Fresh from their first victory under Thomas Frank on Thursday, Crystal Palace welcome Hull City to Selhurst Park in Sunday's matchweek 13 encounter aiming to end their five-match losing league run.

The bottom-placed Eagles sit nine places below their visitors in the Premier League table but hope to draw inspiration from their Europa League success and collect maximum points in the Dane's first home top-flight fixture.

After conceding a late winner against Coventry City on Frank's managerial debut for Palace last weekend, the capital club enjoyed a change of fortune as Dwight McNeil struck in the 81st minute to secure their second European victory.

The winger's goal sealed Palace's first win since beating Fulham in the EFL Cup a month ago, and they now seek consecutive victories for the first time since overcoming the Cottagers and Middlesbrough in the league and domestic cup respectively in early September.

That ambition will be difficult to realise for the Eagles, whose inability to keep clean sheets continues to undermine them, with Mamadou Sarr's 66th-minute goal marking a fifth consecutive match in which the Londoners have conceded.

Their EFL Cup shutout remains Palace's only clean sheet in 11 matches, underlining their broader problems, particularly when they cannot rely on Jean-Philippe Mateta's usual attacking influence.

It remains to be seen whether Frank can address those weaknesses before Sunday's encounter, as the bottom-placed Eagles pursue their first league victory since early October's 3-1 success over Nottingham Forest in an attempt to escape the relegation zone.

Hull's modest scoring figures may not frighten the division's worst defence, but Sergej Jakirovic will know that Coventry were hardly prolific before scoring three in last weekend's 3-2 victory over Palace to reach 13 league goals.

The Tigers also have 13 goals after 11 matches, exceeding Coventry's tally before last weekend and suggesting that the promoted outfit can threaten the division's leakiest defence.

Last season's Championship playoff winners travel to Selhurst Park buoyed by their victory over Brighton & Hove Albion, secured through two goals in second-half stoppage time to end a three-month wait for maximum points in the competition.

That success lifted Jakirovic's team to 11th in the Premier League table, and consecutive victories for the first time since the opening two gameweeks could propel them into the top half, with their 14 points just three short of sixth-placed Brentford.

Having remained difficult to beat throughout their three-month winless spell, Hull now hope to leave any anxiety behind and find the consistency to demonstrate that they belong at this level.

Mateta will serve the final game of his suspension this weekend, while Yeremy Pino is also banned after collecting his fifth yellow card of the season in the defeat to Coventry.

With Ismaila Sarr also unavailable due to a groin problem, the Eagles are missing several potential match-winners and will look to McNeil and Jorgen Strand Larsen, who has already registered one goal and two assists under Frank.

Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) are also sidelined for the hosts on Sunday.

Hull also have several injury concerns: Charlie Hughes will be assessed before the trip to south London, while Hidemasa Morita (muscle), Ilyas Ansah (back), Joe Gelhardt (thigh), Matt Targett (ankle), Eliot Matazo (knee) and Tim Iroegbunam (thigh) are also carrying injuries.

Oli McBurnie and Mohamed Belloumi were instrumental in the Tigers' latest victory, with McBurnie scoring both late goals and Belloumi providing one assist to take their respective goal contributions for the season to six apiece.

Henderson; Khalaili, Richards, Disasi, Mitchell; Timber, Wharton; McNeil, Kamada, Guessand; Strand Larsen

Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Gourna-Douath; Belloumi, Crooks, Thomas; McBurnie

Palace may struggle to build on Thursday's victory without Mateta, Pino and Sarr, particularly with the quick turnaround limiting Frank's preparation time.

Hull remained competitive throughout their prolonged winless spell, and McBurnie's decisive display against Brighton suggests that the visitors could punish another defensive lapse to edge this encounter.

#1674. Como star Paz ‘a wonderful cocktail’, says Fabregas ahead of Juventus clash

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cesc Fabregas described Como Paz as a "wonderful cocktail" as his Como team prepare to face Juventus.

Como, who sit five points ahead of Juventus in Serie A, are enjoying another fantastic season.

Their victory over AEK Athens in midweek lifted them to third in the Champions League standings, while a win over Juve on Sunday would see them climb into the top four in Serie A, ahead of AC Milan playing a day later.

Integral to Como's rise over the past few seasons has been playmaker Paz. In 91 games for the club, he has scored 25 goals, assisted 23 and created 138 chances.

"Nico is physique and talent, vision and mentality," Fabregas told reporters.

"He is a wonderful cocktail, his Mum and Dad did a great job. I used to play in his position, so I like talking to him, to find out if he sees the same things I do.

"At times, I think players don't even need to be coached on movement or control, it's more about tactics.

"The great thing about Nico Paz is he doesn't think about it, he just does the right things.

"Nowadays, we risk creating robots, which helps a certain type of player. However, with Nico, knowing he can make the right choice to win or make the difference, that really helps.

"This is not thanks to my work. We just tried to push him on his mentality and consistency. We are very happy with Nico, and the credit all belongs to him."

It is not just Paz who has thrived under Fabregas' tutelage at Como.

In Europe's big five leagues in 2026-27, only Real Madrid (four) have more players born in 2003 or later with at least three goals than Como (three, level with Roma and Brighton), in Jacobo Ramon, Paz and Martin Baturina.

But Fabregas knows his young stars likely see themselves playing for a bigger club soon enough.

He said: "A young player is like a sponge, he soaks up knowledge. Como is not the apex of their career, they want to go to Manchester City or Juventus. They listen, always want to find space, are very intuitive and ask lots of questions.

"We have a serious, professional attitude here, even when the players are young. When they are ready to take flight and Como is no longer in their plans, that is the moment they will be allowed to fly away, and we will sign someone else."

— Como1907 (@Como_1907) November 25, 2026

Paz has three goals and as many assists in 11 Serie A appearances this season, while he leads Como for chances created in the top flight (19).

Woltemade has been involved in three goals in his last two Serie A games (two goals, one assist) and could be involved in at least one goal in three consecutive league matches for the first time since between September and October 2025 (goals against Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Brighton for Newcastle United in that instance).

Following his goals against Fiorentina and Venezia, he could become the first German player to score in three consecutive Serie A matches since Robin Gosens for Atalanta, between February and March 2021.

Since the start of last November – and Luciano Spalletti's arrival on the Juventus bench – the Bianconeri (19, level with Roma) and Como (20) are two of the three teams with the most clean sheets in Serie A.

Juventus have recorded two wins, two draws and two defeats in their first six away games in Serie A this season, exactly the same record they had away from home at this stage last term (when they suffered a defeat in their seventh away game, 1-2 against Napoli).

The last time the Bianconeri managed fewer than three victories in their first seven away league matches in back-to-back seasons was between 1997-98 and 1999-2000 (two wins, one win and two wins in those three campaigns, respectively).

After their 4-0 triumph over Venezia last time out, Juventus could win two consecutive Serie A matches for only the second time in the last seven months (since the start of last May); the only previous occasion in this period was in the first two matchdays of the current Serie A season (1-0 against Frosinone and 2-0 against Parma).

Como have earned 26 points from their first 12 Serie A matches this season (W8 D2 L2); regardless of the outcome of this game, this is already their record points tally after 13 top-flight games, even considering three-points-for-a-win all-time (24 last season).

Fabregas' team have won both of their last two Serie A matches against Juventus by a 2-0 scoreline; all three of their other victories against the Bianconeri in the competition's history also came in consecutive games without conceding a goal, between November 1950 and January 1952.

This will be the first time in Serie A history that Como will face Juventus while having more points than the Bianconeri at the start of the matchday (+5, 26 to 21).

#1673. Chances to put things right in Europe: The five key battles in Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan will return to a city where they have a glorious history, but this time in dire need of a win to get their European campaign going.

Tonight’s Europa League game against Olympiacos feels a long way away from those Champions League final triumphs in Athens against Barcelona (1994) and Liverpool (2007). However, Ruben Amorim’s side still face a must-win test.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having lost three of four in the UEL thus far, Milan are currently outside even the top 24 places, so they must secure the majority of the remaining 12 points on offer to climb. Their hosts tonight have started much better and are inside the top eight, with 10 points on the board.

Amorim will go with a strong side, or the best possible at least with the injury situation. Pietro Terracciano, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Luka Modric, Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic, Davide Bartesaghi, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Francesco Camarda are all out.

We start with a duel on Milan’s right flank between Diego Moreira and Bruno Onyemaechi. For the Nigerian defender, it will be just his seventh start of the season (out of 15 games played) and this might be arguably his toughest test yet.

Moreira meanwhile has been outstanding in Serie A, with four goals and four assists to his name already. Yet, he hasn’t really got going in Europe yet just like the whole team, given he doesn’t have a goal contribution outside of domestic action. Tonight is a chance to get the ball rolling.

The main threat for Olympiacos is without doubt the attacking midfielder Jota Silva. The former Besiktas man is already on six goals from his 14 appearances (plus one assist) and has really made the No.10 role his. That said, he too is without a goal or assist in Europe so far.

Meanwhile, this is a huge opportunity for Ardon Jashari, as he admitted in his pre-match press conference. The Swiss did very well off the bench against Frosinone and Modric’s injury has opened up a spot for him to take the reins this evening, though he has not always delivered so far when given that task.

Moving back to Milan’s attack, a big night awaits for Goncalo Ramos. He scored in the 4-0 rout of RB Salzburg but is dry in Europe aside from that. The Portuguese ended a one-month goal drought on Sunday by scoring against Frosinone in a move he started and finished, which offers encouragement after a difficult start in red and black.

His opponent will be someone who knows Milan very well, but from the other side of the city. Lorenzo Pirola spent several years in Inter’s academy and has found himself in Athens as one of the leaders of the Olympiacos defence. Tonight will carry a bit of extra meaning, especially amid talk of a potential call-up from Roberto Mancini.

🇵🇹 #Ramos ends his drought! Will a goal like this unlock the #ACMilan striker? 🔓

🎧 Latest podcast: https://t.co/QfaRwdNXza pic.twitter.com/nafNdAUzuL

— SempreMilanTV (@SempreMilanTV) November 25, 2026

Armando Gonzalez is the one who will lead the line for the home side at the Karaiskakis Stadium. The 23-year-old Mexican has scored once so far in the Europa League, but he has three goals overall in four starts and is vying for that starting No.9 position.

Koni De Winter was solid in Sunday’s win meanwhile, and yet he is in need of a performance having really struggled in his battle with Lenny Joseph in the defeat to Ferencvaros last month. The Haitian international – not even their normal starting striker – constantly got the better of the Belgian, who has been up and down in recent weeks.

Finally, we end with the contest between two midfield veterans: Remo Freuler and Adrien Rabiot. The latter has become the anchor of the Erythrolefkoi midfield, and he knows the Rossoneri very well having played for many years in Serie A. The 34-year-old Swiss international also has four assists from a deep-lying playmaker role.

Meanwhile, it has been a tale of two competitions for Rabiot, just like Moreira. The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play, and he actually drew criticism after his performances against Bournemouth and Ferencvaros. It is time to bring that league form onto the continent.

#1672. Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid in advanced talks over new five-year deal - with England superstar set to become one of Europe's HIGHEST earners on par with £500,000-a-week team-mate Vinicius Jr

Published: 17:22 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:40 EST, 23 November 2026

Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid are advancing in talks over a new contract that will make him one of the best paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

Kylian Mbappe remains the best paid player at the club while talks are also advancing over a new contract for Fede Valverde. Real have also recently renewed the contracts of Turkish winger Arda Guler and France international Aurelien Tchouameni on deals until 2032.

Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid are advancing in talks over a contract extension until 2031

The new deal at Madrid will make England's superstar one of the highest earners in Europe - on par with Vinicius Junior's £500,000-a-week contract (Pictured left at his unveiling in 2023)

The contract for Bellingham will be just reward for the 23-year-old who has flourished under coach Jose Mourinho who recently described the former Birmingham City academy graduate as ‘one of a kind’.

1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week

Bellingham, who has scored six goals this season, could be rested for Madrid’s Champions League tie with PSV Eindhoven tonight but was still the topic of conversation as goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois praised his influence on the team on Monday.

‘Jude is someone who really wants to win,’ said Courtois. ‘That's why on the field he swears a lot! He's really a winner, and when he's not happy, he will make it known. He's also a leader on the field. He's a great player, a great mentality. You need those kind of people like that in your team that go for everything.

‘Jude is a young guy but when you see him, it feels like he's a few years older.

‘It seems like he has an engine to play 200 minutes. He keeps on going, running with the ball, it's really hard to dispossess him. And on the outside he just works hard, he goes to the gym. With a good Jude, we play better.’

#1671. Leeds United, Fulham suffer 'extraordinary' blow in pursuit for 11-goal striker target ahead of January window

By Carter White | 27 Nov 2026 14:53, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 15:01

Leeds United and Fulham have reportedly suffered a major blow to their respective pursuits of signing Racing de Santander striker Yassir Zabiri.

Daniel Farke's side have been in the business of getting their own house in order recently, announcing a contract extension for Japanese midfielder Ao Tanaka until the end of the 2028-29 campaign.

Leading Leeds' goalscoring ranks in the Premier League this term, Dominic Calvert-Lewin lead the way for the 28-year-old maestro, with the England international  also signing new terms.

As for matters in West London, Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham went down the La Liga route during the summer transfer window, looking to replace high-profile departures Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson.

It was claimed earlier in the season that members of the Craven Cottage playing staff were unhappy with the situation at the club following the arrival of the former Real Madrid manager.

According to Spanish publication SER Cantabria via El Desmarque, Premier League clubs Leeds and Fulham have suffered a major blow in their potential pursuits of Zaibiri ahead of the January transfer window.

The 21-year-old is currently on loan at Racing Santander from French club Rennes, who supposedly have no option to recall the youngster from his spell in Spain until the end of the season.

The report states that Les Rennais would need to pay Racing Santander an 'extraordinary' amount of compensation to recall Zabiri during the January trading point - a move that would allow a permanent sale of the star.

Leeds, Fulham and Ipswich Town are the known Premier League suitors for the attacker, who recently made his Morocco senior debut during the November international break, scoring against Niger.

However, those English clubs could be blown out of the water by the other horses in this particular transfer race, with Spanish powerhouses Barcelona and Real Madrid said to be interested in the talent.

Netting on 11 occasions across his opening 13 top-flight appearances of the season, Zabiri is only bested by Raphinha (15) and Kylian Mbappe (13) in La Liga's Golden Boot race after 13 games.

The 21-year-old burst onto the Racing Santander stage with a hat-trick against Elche in August before continuing his attacking antics into the autumn, recently bagging a brace in the victory over Real Sociedad.

The world-class form of Zabiri has caught the eye of some of Europe's biggest clubs, so it appears that the likes of Leeds and Fulham are set to be muscled out of a move for the Moroccan sensation.

#1670. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

9 - Erling Haaland is now the top scorer in Premier League games between Manchester City and Manchester United:9 - Haaland (8 apps)8 - Agüero (13 apps)8 - Rooney (21 apps)Domination. pic.twitter.com/EBiifV12st

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

🗣️ "Bruno [Fernandes] is the one who is violent here, I have to call it out"Roy Keane doesn't believe Phil Foden deserved to be sent off against Man Utd 🟥 pic.twitter.com/up5ZQqFShy

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

#MUNMCI – 23'The referee's call of red card to Foden for violent conduct was checked and confirmed by VAR.REF: "Red card Phil Foden – kick out into the body of Bruno".VAR: "That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement. Confirming the red card for…

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

According to The Athletic, the 20-time English champions view Paz as a potential replacement for Fernandes, should the experienced attacker leave Old Trafford.

Journalist David Ornstein claims that Paz is not currently looking to return to Real Madrid, allegedly as he is unsure how much football he would receive due to the presence of Jude Bellingham in the number 10 position at Bernabeu.

Paz shares an agent with new Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, which has also allegedly strengthened the English club's hand when it comes to a potential race.

The attacker is a 16-time Argentina international, scoring six goals and registering two assists for his country, and is currently viewed as one of the best playmakers in world football.

#1668. Brentford’s ‘special group can achieve special things’ – Andrews basks in Old Trafford romp

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keith Andrews believes Brentford have a "special group who can achieve special things" following Saturday's 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United at Old Trafford.

The Bees were ruthless against Mauricio Pochettino's side, who crumbled to their second 4-0 defeat in as many Premier League matches, with Callum Wilson striking twice inside the first half off assists from Dango Ouattara.

Kristoffer Ajer added Brentford's third off another set-up from Ouattara in the 82nd minute before Kevin Schade lobbed Senne Lammens in stoppage time to lift the Bees up to fifth in the Premier League.

And Andrews revelled in a "surreal win", Brentford's first at Old Trafford in 89 years.

"It's slightly surreal if I am honest," Andrews told BBC Match of the Day.

"We have been keen to enjoy the journey. We want to be really ambitious but the level of humility of where we are.

"I think we can achieve special things because I think it is a special group. It has been a good week fofr us and the lads have been excellent.

"A few of us at a certain age are coming to this place and it being a difficult afternoon. So it is never an easy place to come to. The position [United] find themselves in, their manager's first game at home.

"I was keen for us to focus on ourselves and block out that exterior noise and perform like we can. You need to be respectful of where you're coming and the individuals they have.

— Brentford FC (@BrentfordFC) November 28, 2026

"They are dangerous, they are wounded and we expected a reaction. I thought we grew into the game, and we were clinical in the first half. We showed real bravery and courage.

"I was keen for us to block that noise out. It is 11 against 11 on the pitch. We are in a pretty good rhythm and that was the focus."

Brentford have now found the net in 11 of their 12 Premier League matches this season – more than any other side in the division.

Andrews' side have also kept clean sheets in five of their 12 matches, with only Brighton and Arsenal (both seven) managing more shutouts this season.

Wilson, who grabbed his first Premier League goals for Brentford, echoed his manager's sentiment, adding that Brentford's ambitions are sky high.

"Brentford, we're a smaller club that does everything to the maximum of their abilities," Wilson told Sky Sports.

"Everyone on the inside feels they belong at this level. The club's next step in their transition is to win a trophy or step up to Europe.

"It was nice to get off the mark in the league for the club. In [Igor] Thiago's absence, it is about taking opportunities as a striker."
